item.title: F1 makes final call on Qatar and Abu Dhabi amid Middle East situation
item.description: Formula 1 has confirmed that end-of-season races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will go ahead as scheduled. The final two rounds of the 2026 season in Qatar (29 November) and Abu Dhabi (6 December) had been shrouded in uncertainty due to the conflict in the Middle East . Races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia earlier this season were cancelled , though Bahrain did fulfil its event with a one-off race in Malaysia in October. F1 did have the historic Imola circuit as a back-up contingency plan for 6 December, with preliminary grandstand work underway in and around the track site in the Emilia Romagna region of Italy. However, given logistical and freight plans, The Independent understands that F1 has now told Imola to stand down. Qatar and Abu Dhabi will conclude the campaign as planned as part of one final triple-header, starting in Las Vegas on 21 November. An F1 spokesperson added: “We are very grateful for the support and collaboration with the promoter and government in Imola and the region. If the situation develops negatively in the coming weeks before the events in the Middle East we will not hesitate to do the right thing and the safety of everyone will always be the priority.” F1 added that all 11 teams are supportive of concluding the season as planned. The final round of the MotoGP season took place in Qatar – at the same circuit in Lusail, just outside Doha – over the weekend without a hitch, though Yamaha did withdraw from the event pre-race. Nineteen riders also penned a letter expressing their wish not to race in Qatar, but both races were held as planned. Previous UK travel guidance during the height of the US/Israel-Iran conflict this year advised against “all but essential” travel to Qatar and Abu Dhabi. However, that has since been lifted, with tension in the region cooling in recent weeks. That being said, the UK’s Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) does state that the “broader security context” in the Middle East “carries a risk of sudden escalation, potential flight cancellations and airspace disruptions.” Both F1 chief Stefano Domenicali and FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem have insisted in recent weeks that the Middle Eastern races will take place as planned, barring any sudden re-escalation of hostilities in the region. Moto GP finished their season in Qatar on Sunday (Reuters) Mercedes boss Toto Wolff, whose team clinched the constructors’ championship in Brazil last weekend, a week after Kimi Antonelli won the drivers’ title, has backed the sport to make the right call. "Stefano and Mohamme have been pretty clear about the situation that Formula 1 follows what the international guidelines are, whether there are travel restrictions, airlines not flying, any warnings in the region, the kind of feedback that local governments are making," Wolff said. "So not only the promoters, but what the local governments are making. And this is what you need to rely on, in my opinion, and I'm fully with that. "I think that if [Mot

item.title: “Doesn’t Hurt That You Have $50M+”: Kyle Whittingham Shifts Attention to Oregon’s Massive Recruiting Budget Ahead of Ducks Clash
item.description: Michigan football head coach Kyle Whittingham speaks as he is being introduced on the floor during the first half between Michigan and USC at Crisler Center © Imagn Michigan football is at a crossroads as it aims to rescue its college football season, and the pressure is on Kyle Whittingham. The Wolverines’ head coach made the decision to fire offensive coordinator Jason Beck after an unsatisfactory run of performances, but he still needs to win games to keep his own job secure. Ahead of the game against the Oregon Ducks, who are themselves turning a corner after some tough results, Whittingham shifted attention to Oregon’s massive recruiting budget, highlighting the difference between the two sides. “He really does a great job recruiting and it doesn’t hurt that you have $50+ million dollars at your disposal to, in essence outbid everybody. Not everybody, but a lot of people. But that’s not his fault,” Whittingham said about head coach Dan Lanning to reporters, via Inside Michigan . He further said that he meant it as a credit to the program and its desire to focus on young athletes in the NIL era. “That’s a credit. I mean, that’s a credit to their program and their dedication and desire to win and the support they have. NIL is the name of the game in recruiting these days. It’s shifted so much,” he went on. Kyle Whittingham Explained Why He Fired Jason Beck After a tough defeat to Michigan State, offensive coordinator Jason Beck received his marching orders from Kyle Whittingham, and he addressed the decision to media personnel. “Well, watching the film really was the deciding factor, and I had the intention of waiting until after the season, as I mentioned,” Whittingham said to reporters, as reported by Wolverines Wire . He further revealed when it became completely clear to him that a change was needed. “But when I turned the film on and really dove into it, it just became apparent to me that you need to make the change now. And there’s just too much regression in the offense in that particular game. And that’s what led to the decision.” Whittingham also confirmed no other person was involved in making the decision but himself. The decision will be put to the test as the Wolverines play the Oregon Ducks on Saturday. item.title: Greyson Fuller's 1,000-yard season is only a first step to become South's next great QB
item.description: EAST STROUDSBURG – Is Greyson Fuller the next great East Stroudsburg South quarterback? The jury is still out, but the junior signal-caller took the first step towards earning that distinction. Fuller, who completed his first season as the full-time starter for the Cavaliers after stepping up as a sophomore in 2025, became the 17 th South QB to throw for at least 1,000 yards in a single season, finishing the 2026 campaign with 1,767 yards. He nearly reached this milestone last season after filling in for an injured Ivan Laubach, but now the milestone is officially his. “It feels great,” Fuller said about the accomplishment. “I grew up looking at the banner hanging in the gym of all the 1,000-yard guys, and it’s going to be awesome seeing my name up there.” Going to the 'ship: East football avenges Bucket Game loss, beats PV to advance to 5A district title game South head coach Matt Walters has consistently commended Fuller’s development from his sophomore year to his junior year, and he’s proud of how he reached the milestone. As great as the milestone is, however, it’s only a first step on the path to be among the program greats. Granted, Fuller’s 1,767 yards rank him seventh all-time in program history for single-season passing yards, and 15 th all-time amongst all Pocono quarterbacks. But here are the fellow Cavaliers ahead of him: Jake Cirillo, who threw for 1,000 yards all four years of high school before going to play for East Stroudsburg University Ivan Laubach, a 2,000-yard passer who led South to a district championship. Bobby McClosky, an EPC North MVP, and a First Team All-State Selection And Rob Moyer, the area’s all-time leader in single-season passing yards, and the only player in Pocono history to pass for 2,000 yards twice Even some of the names behind Fuller who lack in numbers make up for the difference in accolades. ESU head coach Jimmy Terwilliger was the first East Stroudsburg (before the split) quarterback to have multiple 1,000-yard seasons, and he did that with a coach who ran the option in the legend Ed Christian. Oh yeah, and he later earned the honor of the best player in Division II football. And there’s also Will Fish, who joined the 1,000-yard club in 2019 and nearly threw for 2,000 his junior year and went on to play at Lycoming College. Fish is now on staff at South, where he watched Fuller throw for 303 passing yards and five touchdowns against Pocono Mountain West. “Coach Fish talked to me on the sidelines midgame and asked me how many touchdowns I was at,” Fuller said. “He then said, ‘All right, my record is six touchdowns. You got to see if you can beat that.’ It's a different standard that that I'm being held to, and I think that's awesome. “I'm always being pushed to do more no matter what milestone I reach.” Walters has witnessed nearly all of East Stroudsburg South’s football history, from growing up in the area, to being an assistant under Christian, to now serving as head coach. item.description: Alisson Becker acknowledges the Liverpool supporters singing his name after his superb performance in the win at Crystal Palace -Credit:Steve Bardens - AMA/Getty Images The November international break has arrived, but business continues at Liverpool as the club presses ahead with plans to strengthen under Andoni Iraola. While the manager focuses on improvements on the training pitch during the two-week hiatus, the recruitment department will also be working diligently to identify external options capable of making a real impact on the team going forward. That could encompass moves in the upcoming January transfer window or potential long-term targets for the summer window, while internal discussions will also center on several critical contract situations. With that in mind, here's a rundown of the latest Liverpool transfer news and rumors ahead of another busy day for the Reds. Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac address Wrexham executive’s abrupt exit USMNT legend Alexi Lalas on Mauricio Pochettino to Man Utd links amidst pressure on Michael Carrick Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker has revealed that his agent is in negotiations with the club regarding his future, as the shot-stopper approaches the final few months of his deal, which runs out next summer. Speaking to Liverpool.com and a group of reporters following the weekend's match against Crystal Palace, the Brazilian stated: "I'm focused on playing every game, but in my mind I'm happy to stay. You know, that depends on a lot of aspects and different situations. But my will is to stay.", reports Liverpool.com . "I'm happy here, my family is happy here. I'm still hungry for titles and for delivering good performances. I still want to play at the top level for as long as I can. So that's my thinking on that." When pressed on whether discussions were ongoing with Liverpool, he said: "My agent is talking with the club." Liverpool.com reports: Alisson's performances have been inconsistent this season, yet when called into action, the goalkeeper has largely delivered when it mattered most. Goalkeepers can typically continue playing at a high level for longer than outfield players, suggesting there may be less risk involved in handing the Brazilian a new contract compared to other veteran stars within the squad. There may be reasonable concerns regarding wage expectations versus on-field output, particularly if Alisson's standards decline significantly, but ultimately it will come down to negotiations. The only additional factor to consider may be the players behind him, with Giorgi Mamardashvili widely expected to step up around this period to claim the number one jersey. With several months still remaining, Liverpool are under no immediate pressure to rush into offering a new contract, but early dialogue is an encouraging indicator that progress can be made. item.title: ESPN Names Eagles TE as Potential ‘Luxury Target’ for Seattle Seahawks
item.description: The Seattle Seahawks could explore adding another tight end before the NFL trade deadline, with Dallas Goedert emerging as a potential luxury target, according to ESPN. The Philadelphia Eagles veteran could provide an additional receiving option as Seattle looks to address an injury at the position and strengthen its offense. The Seahawks have a need following Elijah Arroyo’s injury, which leaves the team with another reason to consider reinforcements. Adding an experienced tight end would give quarterback Sam Darnold another dependable target, while Drew Lock could also benefit if he takes over under center. Dec 14, 2025; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert (88) scores a touchdown during the third quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Goedert could become available if Philadelphia decides to make changes during what could be a transitional period for the organization. The Eagles may consider moving the veteran rather than retaining him for the remainder of a season in which their postseason outlook could influence their roster decisions. His contract could make a potential deal particularly appealing for Seattle. Goedert is playing on a one-year agreement and is due just $650,000 for the remainder of the 2026 season, giving the Seahawks a relatively affordable opportunity to add an established player without taking on a significant financial commitment. ESPN’s NFL Analysis Names Dallas Goedert as Seattle Seahawks Potential Luxury Target Jan 15, 2024; Tampa, Florida, USA; Philadelphia Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert (88) reacts during the second half of a 2024 NFC wild card game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-USA TODAY Sports Goedert was named as Seattle’s possible luxury target before the NFL trade deadline . This is detailed more in an analysis by Bill Barnwell for ESPN. Luxury target: Adding another tight end to replace injured Elijah Arroyo and give Darnold (or Drew Lock) another reliable pass catcher would be one way to improve the offense. An Eagles team in a soft rebuild could move on from Dallas Goedert, who is on a one-year deal and due only $650,000 over the remainder of 2026. Goedert is one year removed from an 11-touchdown season, so having a second option near the goal line and in the red zone beyond Smith-Njigba would be enough to justify Goedert’s salary. The veteran also brings a history of production that could address one of Seattle’s offensive needs. He recorded 11 touchdowns in a season just one year ago, demonstrating his ability to contribute near the goal line. That experience could give the Seahawks another option in scoring situations, particularly when defenses focus on limiting Jaxon Smith-Njigba. item.title: Hull City's Oli McBurnie opens up on emotional Scotland return under Pocognoli
item.description: Scotland manager Sebastien Pocognoli greets Oli McBurnie at Hampden Park -Credit:Andrew Milligan/PA Wire Striker Oli McBurnie has recalled the deeply personal moment he received the call from new Scotland manager Sébastien Pocognoli, confirming his international comeback after five years in exile. The Hull City forward had nearly abandoned hopes of ending his international drought under previous head coach Steve Clarke, despite netting 19 goals for the Tigers, including the crucial Wembley goal that secured the club's Premier League promotion, having been overlooked for the World Cup. McBurnie concluded his club commitments on Saturday following the Tigers' tight 1-0 defeat at Arsenal, with focus now shifting to two pivotal Nations League fixtures at home against North Macedonia on Friday night, before traveling to Switzerland on Monday evening. Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac address Wrexham executive’s abrupt exit USMNT legend Alexi Lalas on Mauricio Pochettino to Man Utd links amidst pressure on Michael Carrick "He (Pocognoli) FaceTimed me; he messaged me, asking if I was free," the City forward recalls in conversation with Hull Live. "I was just sat at home with the kids and the missus, and he FaceTimed me out of the blue and told me about his plans and what he'd been watching and what he'd seen in me and what he'd wanted his teams to be and them sort of thing. "We had a good chat, and then he told me that I was going to be in. It was, it was hard for me to keep the smile off my face, and yeah, it was, it was a really nice moment.", reports Hull Live . Make sure you never miss the latest Hull City news and opinion by making Hull Live one of your Google preferred sources. "He's (Pocognoli) been brilliant. While we were away, I learnt a lot about him. The thing is, with internationals, they have so little time to implement their game plan. You have 25 lads coming from 25 different teams that all play a different way, and then you have a week of training. It's gonna take time, but yeah, I was really impressed with the manager and his ideas, and yeah, really impressed. "My missus was in the room with the kids, so she heard it, so I didn't have to tell them because they heard it. I was trying to tell my little one; she didn't quite get it. She knows Hull as the Tigers cos she likes tigers, and Scotland has a lion on it, so the Lions. That's the way she knows. They came up, watched the games that were at Hampden. "All the things now that you do is for your kids, so my kids have been able to see me represent my country. It was something I never thought they'd get to see. I've played however many times for Scotland before, and it was something that I never thought they'd get to see their old man playing for the country. To get to see their old man playing in the Premier League and playing for his country as well. It was nice for me and for them to see that." item.title: Managerial 'inconsistency' hurting Ghana - Hughton
item.description: Kim Bjorkegren (right) is in interim charge of Ghana after Carlos Queiroz left the Black Stars by mutual consent [Getty Images] As Ghana prepare for two make-or-break 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) qualifiers with women's coach Kim Bjorkegren in temporary charge, former boss Chris Hughton has called for greater consistency in the Black Stars dugout. The West Africans face Somalia in back-to-back fixtures over the next week, having lost their first two games in Group C against Ivory Coast and The Gambia last month. Those defeats resulted in the departure of Carlos Queiroz, whose brief period in the hot seat was characterised by uncertainty. The Portuguese's exit means Swede Bjorkegren, who has been in charge of the Black Queens since January 2025, has now been asked to lead the men's team against Somalia. "When you have inconsistency in the amount of time when a manager is staying, it's never good," Hughton told BBC Sport Africa. "You want that consistency in the players [and] the players want that consistency in what they see in the manager." Queiroz, who had two spells as Sir Alex Ferguson's assistant at Manchester United, was initially appointed in April and led Ghana to the last 32 of the Fifa World Cup, holding England to a goalless draw in the group stage, before announcing his own departure shortly after the team were eliminated 1-0 by Colombia in the last 32. However, the 73-year-old was reappointed in early September, with the Ghana Football Association (GFA) praising his "extensive international experience" gained during time in charge of South Africa, Egypt, Portugal, Iran, Colombia, Qatar and Oman. But Queiroz's return lasted less than a month following a 2-0 defeat by the Ivorians in Bouake and a 4-2 humbling against the Gambians in front of home fans in Accra. "What I saw in the World Cup is that they represented the country very well, particularly the England game," said Hughton. "And although it was very much a defensive outfit, there were opportunities to score." Hughton, however, admits that regular sackings can create an "attitude" within a squad, with players knowing that "if he (the coach) doesn't do well then he won't be there". Ex-Brighton boss Hughton reveals cancer diagnosis Ex-Brighton boss Hughton backs mental health drive Ghana's managerial merry-go-round Ghana suffered group-stage exits at the 2021 and 2023 Afcons under Milovan Rajevac (left) and Chris Hughton (right) before failing to qualify for the 2025 edition under Otto Addo (right) [Getty Images] Hughton's Ghana reign was also short lived. Appointed as technical director by the GFA in February 2022, he moved into the head coach role in February 2023 but lasted less than 12 months before being sacked in January 2024 after his team failed to get out of their group at the 2023 Afcon in Ivory Coast. item.title: Jordan Davis reveals why he's 'disappointed' after Eagles trade with Jaguars
item.description: Jordan Davis reveals why he's 'disappointed' after Eagles trade with Jaguars originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Eagles made one of the more surprising moves of the NFL trade deadline when they traded beloved defensive tackle Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars . A lot of the focus had been on Moro Ojomo and even Jalen Carter as trade targets. Instead, it was Davis who was dealt from this DT room. For Eagles fans, it's sad to see Davis go after he became a fan favorite in Philadelphia. But how is Davis handling it? According to Jeff Skversky for FOX 29 Philadelphia , Davis shared that he's "disappointed" in the trade and revealed why. Why Jordan Davis is 'disappointed' after Eagles-Jaguars trade "A little disappointed, but understanding that they're in a rebuilding process, and you know for the price, first-round, second-round pick, you know, obviously helps the team... I love those guys, so however I can help the team in my departure, I'm absolutely glad to be doing that," Davis said. “Disappointed” 💔Jordan Davis tells me in an exclusive 1-on-1 interview after being traded to the Jags he loves the Eagles & Philly will always have a special place in his heart but he understands the #Eagles are “rebuilding” More on @FOX29philly ▶️https://t.co/7Q5pvUjXA0 https://t.co/MBk4dpLEKS — Jeff Skversky (@JeffSkversky) November 10, 2026 The beloved defensive tackle is disappointed about being traded to the Jaguars, as he obviously still loves the Eagles and wants to help the team. His admission that he's glad to help the Eagles, in the form of the compensation he was able to bring back to the franchise, being something that he's glad he could do shows just how much he loves the Eagles. MORE : Jaguars reportedly acquiring Falcons' Pro Bowl safety in major trade Davis isn't disappointed about joining the Jaguars, a team that has a very real chance of winning a Super Bowl this season. He's just disappointed about leaving the Eagles. But with the Eagles' 2-7 record, Jalen Hurts being out for the season and uncertain to play again, and Lane Johnson retired, it's time for the Eagles to shift gears. Unfortunately, part of the fallout from this down season is some players being traded away, with Cam Jurgens going earlier in the year and now Davis being dealt to the Jaguars for a 2027 first- and 2029 second-round pick. Just as Eagles fans were disappointed in the Davis trade, so too is the fan-favorite lineman. But both sides know that this is a good move for the Eagles, as the compensation from the Jaguars is worthwhile to trade away Davis. item.title: Vikings vs. Packers odds: Vikings underdogs heading into Lambeau
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 09: Christian Benford #47 of the Buffalo Bills breaks up a pass intended for Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings during the first quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 09, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images After falling out of first place in the NFC North for the first time this season, the Minnesota Vikings will look to avoid moving into the division’s basement when they head to Lambeau Field in Week 10 to conclude their home-and-home series with the Green Bay Packers for this season. The people who set the betting lines, apparently, don’t like their chances. Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the lines for Sunday’s game, and the Vikings currently sit as a 4.5-point underdog to the Packers. The over/under for the game currently rests at 42.5 points. The Vikings, as we all saw on Monday Night Football, appear to have completely abandoned the concept of offense, as they generated none of it in a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills for their second loss in a row. Carson Wentz stepped in at quarterback for the injured Kyler Murray and turned in what may have been the worst start a Vikings quarterback has put together in recent memory, completing just 8-of-25 passes and turning the ball over three times, including two interceptions. . .a number that could have been significantly higher. The Packers, on the other hand, have won five of their last six after getting off to a 1-2 start. This past week, they absolutely thumped the New England Patriots to the tune of 45-27 behind three more touchdown passes from Jordan Love and a defense that forced Drake Maye into three interceptions. The Packers currently sit in last place in the North, but with a 6-3 record would lead either the NFC South or the NFC East. . .that’s just how good the NFC North has been this season. These two teams met in the regular season opener at U.S. Bank Stadium. Wentz came into the game midway through the first quarter after Murray suffered a concussion, and the Packers had a 22-10 lead with just over five minutes remaining in the third quarter. From there, however, the Minnesota defense took over, leading an onslaught against Love and the Green Bay offense that saw the Vikings score 29 unanswered points to finish the game, including forcing a turnover on downs and generating an interception and a fumble to set up scoring opportunities. Minnesota took home the 39-22 win to get their season off to a 1-0 start. With the NFL trade deadline looming at 3:00 PM Central today. . .or approximately seven hours from when this story goes up. . .we will see if anything the Vikings do (or don’t do) will shift this number at all. As it stands now, however, the Vikings are currently an underdog to their division rivals as the second half of the season officially gets underway.

item.title: FIA boss looks to ‘end age limits’ for office holders – six months after ditching term limits
item.description: Mohammed Ben Sulayem is reportedly looking to end age limits for FIA office holders – just six months after the FIA president ditched term limits for those in leadership posts. Emirati executive Ben Sulayem, 64, has been FIA president since December 2021 and was re-elected last year after other candidates were prevented from standing, due to quirks in the FIA statutes which meant the only prospective vice-president in one region was already aligned with Ben Sulayem. Currently, FIA statutes rule out anyone over the age of 75 from standing for a presidential term. This rule was implemented in 2024 to “modernise the governance of the FIA and ensure that candidates for the presidency are more aligned with current leadership practices.” Yet just six months after Ben Sulayem ended term limits for those in leadership posts, the BBC reports that Ben Sulayem wants to discontinue the age-limit rule and put forward a proposal detailing as such to the FIA’s General Assembly in Shanghai next month. An FIA spokesperson told The Independent: “An age limit excludes candidates solely on the basis of their date of birth, regardless of their experience, expertise, or ability to contribute. Ultimately, the competent FIA bodies will retain full authority to elect the officeholders they deem appropriate.” “The proposal to remove age limits for FIA officeholders is one of the proposed amendments to the FIA Statutes to be put to the General Assembly in Shanghai in December. It was approved by the World Councils for submission in line with the process set out in the FIA Statutes, and will only take effect if the General Assembly votes in favour.” Ben Sulayem had originally introduced an upper age limit of 70 in 2023, in a move widely seen to prevent Motorsport UK boss David Richards from running. Ben Sulayem, who is a regular in parc ferme and on the podium after F1 races, has overseen controversial moments in his near-five years in charge. Ben Sulayem has clashed with Max Verstappen in the past (Getty) His first term saw Ben Sulayem clash with Lewis Hamilton over the Brit’s desire to wear jewellery in the cockpit, while he also angered drivers, including four-time world champion Max Verstappen, for issuing fines for swearing. Last April, Robert Reid resigned as deputy president for sport, accusing the governing body of a "breakdown in governance standards." And presidential candidates such as Tim Mayer and Laura Villars were unhappy after they could not oppose him in last year’s presidential elections. FIA rules dictate a vice-president candidate must be nominated from each of its six global regions; Bernie Ecclestone’s wife, Fabiana, the sole South American candidate, supported Ben Sulayem. Meanwhile, Ben Sulayem has also voiced his support for end-of-season races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi to go ahead. A final call is expected on Tuesday.

item.title: Jazz Chisholm Jr. Faces Short Deal Path Like Bo Bichette
item.description: Pablo Robles-Imagn Images Jazz Chisholm Jr. is not going to get the same big money that Bo Bichette secured in free agency last year. Bichette left the Toronto Blue Jays for a three-year, $126 million pact with the New York Mets. The Bichette pact averages out to $42 million per year. The key to that massive contract was the opt-out clauses Bichette added after each season. He could have hit the open market this winter but chose to stay, and he holds that same power again next year. Chisholm now faces a similar path to get his value right, though the market looks much tougher for him. A Tough Market for a Talented Player USA Today’s Bob Nightengale wrote a piece on Monday about ten free agents who will draw close attention soon. He looked specifically at Chisholm’s situation and the idea of using an opt-out clause. Nightengale wrote that “He could be in for a rude awakening in the free agent market with executives openly wondering if anyone would give him more than a two-year contract.” The Yankees did not make a qualifying offer to Chisholm, so he is now a free agent. This means teams can sign him without paying a draft pick to New York, but it also signals the team is ready to move on if the price is too high. Despite the rough talk from front offices, Chisholm brings real skills to the table. He is a year removed from a 30/30 season where he hit 30 home runs and stole 30 bases. In 2026, he set a career high with 41 stolen bases in 50 attempts. That speed was a bright spot even if his overall hitting numbers were down. He has played second base since the trade from the Marlins and has graded out well there based on defensive metrics. He also has experience playing center field. His talent is undeniable, but teams worry about his consistency over a long term. Experts Predict a Reset Strategy Nightengale noted that “No one can debate his talent. He may need an opt-out on any multi-year proposal so he can hit market again and re-establish himself.” This strategy mirrors what Bichette did. If Chisholm signs for two years, he can prove he is healthy and hitting, then test the market again for a bigger deal. Various outlets have different guesses on what he might get. According to reports, Chisholm’s potential deals are either 3 years/$110 million or 7 years/$185 million. Fangraphs, including Ben Clemens and the median crowdsource, has him at 4 years and $92 million. Kiley McDaniel sees a 2-year, $46 million deal with an opt-out, while MLB Trade Rumors has him at 2 years and $40 million with an opt-out. The Philadelphia Phillies are one team that might make a move for him. Just Baseball’s Ryan Finkelstein forecasts that Chisholm will agree to a two-year, $40 million deal with Philadelphia this offseason. For the 2027 season, Finkelstein stated Chisholm would earn $25 million, followed by a $15 million player option in 2028. Finkelstein wrote that “The best case for Jazz is likely a 1+1 deal where he can reset his market and have a pillow of a player

item.title: Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph won't make return in Germany
item.description: Kerby Joseph's season debut won't come on foreign soil. Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell said in his weekly radio interview on 97.1 The Ticket (WXYT-FM) that Joseph will not play in this weekend's game against the New England Patriots in Germany. Joseph remains on the physically unable to perform list recovering from a cartilage condition in his knee that has kept him out of game action since last October. He returned to practice Oct. 28, and the Lions have until next week to activate him to the 53-man roster or keep him on PUP for the rest of the year. Campbell has tempered expectations for Joseph's return, though both he and safeties coach Jim O'Neill said Joseph had a good week of practice last week. The Lions traded for backup safety Andre Cisco on Monday, Nov. 9, adding him to a position group that includes starters Brian Branch and Chuck Clark, rookie backup Keith Abney and special teams player Christian Izien. BIRKETT: 10 players Detroit Lions could target for upgrades "It gives us flexibility," Campbell said of the Cisco trade. "That’s what it does do is Cisco’s obviously safety, he played nickel, he can play other things on third down in your dime package. So can Branch. We get Kerby back eventually here, Kerby gives you flexibility, you keep him where you need him or move him back and forth." The Lions (6-2) play two games in five days once they return from Germany, against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Nov. 22 and the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving. O'Neil said last week the team had not determined how to work Joseph back in the lineup once he is activated to the 53-man roster. More from Campbell's radio interview Campbell touched on a couple other topics in his weekly interview Tuesday. Asked about Christian Mahogany's benching last week for violating team rules, Campbell indicated Mahogany has done that multiple times this year. "That's why I have team rules, that's why we have team rules and we all got to abide by them, and if it's broken multiple times, then you do something about it," Campbell said. "We're on good standing and like I said, the ball's in his court. It'll be good." Asked how Mahogany has responded since his benching, Campbell said, "Listen, we're good. We're all good. He'll be fine." "Look, if you say you're going to do something, you better hold up to it or otherwise you're going to lose the respect of people around you," Campbell said. "Because if I'm sitting in that seat and I say one thing and then I don't do it, I'll immediately lose respect for that person. So we stick by what we say we're going to do here." More deals? On Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, Campbell did not directly answer a question about whether the Lions are close to making any more deals, like they were two years ago when news of the Za'Darius Smith trade broke during Campbell's radio interview. "No, we’re not going to trade for Za’Darius, and as of right now there’s nothing that I’ve heard in the last 10 minutes," Campbell said. When asked a foll

item.title: Former Royals catcher and manager Bob Boone dies at age 78
item.description: BOSTON, MA - MAY 22: Bob Boone #8 of the Kansas City Royals takes a swing during a baseball game against the Boston Red Sox on May 22, 1989 at Fenway Park in Boston, Massachusetts. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bob Boone, a four-time All-Star catcher who spent two seasons as a player with the Kansas City Royals before managing the club for parts of three seasons, has died at the age of 78, according to a social media post from his family . The son of All-Star infielder Ray Boone, and the father of All-Star infielders Bret and Aaron Boone, the Boones were the first family to have three generations of MLB players. RIP Bob Boone, the great Gold Glove, All Star and World Series champion catcher, who passes away at 78. Condolences to wife Sue and sons Aaron and Bret Boone. What a marvelous man and privilege and honor to know. — Bob Nightengale (@BNightengale) November 10, 2026 Bob Boone was one of the most accomplished defensive catchers of his generation, winning seven Gold Glove Awards over a 19-year playing career. He was originally drafted by the Philadelphia Phillies after a standout career at Stanford. He he finished third in Rookie of the Year voting and was a three-time All-Star with the Phillies. He faced the Royals in the 1980 World Series as a catcher for the Phillies, hitting .412 (7-for-17) in the series for his only championship. He moved onto the Angels in 1982, helping them win the division in their first year, earning MVP votes, and winning a Gold Glove. He was an All-Star the next year, and over seven years in Anaheim, he set the club record for most games behind the plate. He left Anaheim and signed with the Royals in 1989 at the age of 41. He appeared in 131 games and hit .274/.351/.323, winning his seventh Gold Glove and finishing with 2.4 rWAR. After 40 games in 1990, he retired. After the 1994 season was cancelled during the work stoppage, the Royals hired Bob Boone as manager to replace Hal McRae and usher in a new youth movement. Despite trading away stars like David Cone and Brian McRae, the Royals were in the hunt for the new “Wild Card” spot for most of the season, until a poor September caused them to fall under .500 at 70-74. Boone was a very cerebral manager, but would frequently clash with the media. He was criticized for constantly changing the lineup, and for employing “Boonieball,” as then-Kansas City Star columnist Jeffrey Flanagan would call his style of play. Boone finished just 75-86 in 1996, and was fired at the 1997 All-Star break after a 36-46 start, replaced by Tony Muser. Boone would later manage the Cincinnati Reds from 2001-2003, although he never managed them to a winning season. He joined the Washington Nationals front office in 2005 and served the team until he retired in 2021.

item.title: US university suspends fraternity after students filmed on fire
item.description: Ohio State University in the United States has suspended a fraternity after footage emerged showing two young men on fire, local media reported on Monday. The video, which garnered more than 1.5 million views on X, shows the pair surrounded by a group laughing and filming as they roll around on the ground, engulfed in flames. Fraternities — male social clubs common on US campuses — have long come under scrutiny for booze-infused parties and hazing rituals that can lead to sexual assault, accidents and even deaths. The elite Cornell University suspended fraternity parties and social events last month for the remaining academic year following an alleged gang rape at one of its clubs that has horrified Americans. “The university is aware of this extremely concerning incident, and the individuals in question are receiving needed medical care,” Ohio State University spokesman Ben Johnson said in a statement quoted by local news outlet WCMH-TV. “Ohio State has placed the Sigma Alpha Epsilon fraternity on interim suspension pending a full investigation.” Sigma Alpha Epsilon claims on its website to have “forged men into leaders” since its foundation in 1856. Columbus police said they were also investigating the incident. The post US university suspends fraternity after students filmed on fire appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: USMNT could lose head coach just months after signing extension
item.description: Soccer Football - FIFA World Cup 2026 - United States Press Conference - Los Angeles Stadium, Inglewood, California, U.S. - June 11, 2026 U.S. coach Mauricio Pochettino during the press conference REUTERS/Daniel Cole Manchester United have gotten off to the worst start in their Premier League history, and it looks like Michael Carrick is about to pay the price. The club is reportedly ready to fire its manager, with United sitting in the relegation zone after just one win in 10 league games. And United’s top choice to replace him could come as a big blow to American soccer fans. U.S. men’s national team head coach Mauricio Pochettino is reportedly the favorite for the job, less than four months after signing a contract extension with U.S. Soccer. Pochettino and the USMNT Pochettino took over the USMNT in 2024 with the goal of leading the team on a deep run in the World Cup on home soil. Instead, the U.S. was eliminated in the Round of 16 by Belgium in a blowout loss. That run also came with its share of controversy. Pochettino later admitted it was a “mistake” after FIFA overturned a suspension to Folarin Balogun ahead of the Belgium match, a decision that came after President Donald Trump said he had contacted FIFA president Gianni Infantino about it. He also didn’t mince words about Christian Pulisic’s struggles. Still, U.S. Soccer stood by Pochettino after the tournament, and in August, it announced that he had signed a new deal that runs through the 2030 World Cup. Manchester United’s Interest According to ESPN’s Mark Ogden and Rob Dawson , United’s leadership, including co-chairman Joel Glazer and minority owner Jim Ratcliffe, has been assessing Carrick’s future. Sources told ESPN that there is “now acceptance that performances and results demand a change of manager.” Carrick took over as interim manager in January and led United to Champions League qualification, earning a two-year contract this summer. But the club has won just one of four games since giving him time to turn things around last month, leaving United one point off the bottom of the table. Pochettino, who has interviewed for the United job three times before, is regarded as having “the Premier League experience and personality needed to drag United out of danger,” per the report. The former Tottenham, Chelsea, and PSG manager also reportedly has a $10 million escape clause in his U.S. Soccer contract, which United would have to pay. Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann, and Kieran McKenna are also reportedly among the candidates. United’s next match is against Liverpool at Anfield on Nov. 22. Needless to say, U.S. Soccer will be watching this one closely. The post USMNT could lose head coach just months after signing extension appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Michael Carrick takes training as Man Utd hierarchy ponders his future
item.description: Michael Carrick took training on Tuesday as Manchester United ’s powerbrokers drag their heels over the beleaguered head coach’s future ahead of a key meeting in Monaco. The former midfielder’s days in charge appear to be numbered after overseeing the club’s worst start to a campaign since 1986, leaving the Red Devils in the relegation zone over the international break. United, who languish in 18th, are using the two-week hiatus to review Carrick’s position and consider alternatives, with the head coach widely expected to lose his job following discussions. But Old Trafford sources remained adamant on Tuesday lunchtime that no decision had been made after the 45-year-old reported to the Carrington training complex earlier that day to take training. Carrick’s future is set to be decided 800 miles away from Manchester in Monaco, where director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada are due to give their views to United’s ownership. A meeting is reportedly scheduled in the principality on Wednesday with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe , whose Ineos company controls football operations and would sign off a change at the top with the Glazers. United are keeping tight-lipped on the process and relevant meetings, which is only prolonging the agony for popular former midfielder Carrick, who made 464 appearances for the club between 2006 and 2018. Michael Carrick (left) was part of Manchester United’s triumphant Champions League side in 2008 (Owen Humphreys/PA) Mauricio Pochettino , the former Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea boss, has emerged as the leading contender to replace him . The former Argentina international has held talks with United in the past and is understood to be interested in the Old Trafford post, but hefty compensation would be due for the United States boss. Just three months ago Pochettino and his staff extended their deals until 2030 and are currently in Georgia preparing for Nations League quarter-final fixtures against Haiti on Saturday and Tuesday. Aston Villa boss Unai Emery is admired, while ex-Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and former Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann were linked a fortnight ago when United seriously considered replacing Carrick. US boss Mauricio Pochettino is interested in the United job (Adam Davy/PA) A 4-1 Champions League loss at Como and 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth left the head coach’s job hanging by a thread, but the club decided to give him the opportunity to turn the situation around. Carrick’s side subsequently lost 2-0 at Chelsea, where they were unable to take their chances and saw Lisandro Martinez sent off, before last Tuesday’s thrilling 3-2 Champions League comeback win against Roma. A scarcely believable 4-4 draw against Aston Villa followed on Sunday, after which the head coach stressed he would not walk away and was looking to the international break as usual. item.title: Chelsea named as one of three teams interested in £60m January move for Premier League winner
item.description: Chelsea named as one of three teams interested in £60m January move for Premier League winner Chelsea are one of three teams being most strongly linked to Martin Zubimendi of Arsenal ahead of a potential January move. If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content. Well connected reporter Miguel Delaney of the Independent has today written a long story about the future of Martin Zubimendi at Arsenal. The former Real Sociedad man signed for the Gunners in the summer of 2025 but has never established himself as an untouchable player. He’s now apparently up for sale, with a move in January possible. Chelsea, Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid are all named as potential destinations by Delaney. Chelsea consider £60m January move for Arsenal man Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images) His current coach Mikel Arteta sees Zubimendi as a “valuable option”, but favours Bruno Guimaraes, Declan Rice and Myles Lewis Skelly ahead of him. Arsenal would like to sign a winger, and accept that selling Zubimendi is the best way to fund that. They want to “at least” recoup the £60m they paid for him. Chelsea’s midfield currently has Moises Caicedo as the undisputed starter, with Romeo Lavia and Jordan Henderson starting alongside him in recent games. Zubimendi would certainly be seen as an upgrade on the 36 year old England midfielder. Youngsters like Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli are regularly named on the bench and featured in the Carabao Cup in central midfield in earlier rounds. Alex Scott is regularly linked as another potential signing. In other news… Chelsea are now 10 games into the Xabi Alonso era, and some fans and pundits are starting to get upset about a lack of progress.

item.title: Escalating CNG Prices: FG Threatens Sanctions Against Marketers Exploiting Unsuspecting Nigerians
item.description: The Federal Government has threatened to sanction marketers exploiting unsuspecting Nigerians over escalating prices of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) across the country. Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Gas), Ekperikpe Ekpo, spoke on Tuesday in Kano during the inspection of some CNG mother station infrastructure ahead of the commissioning of the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano AKK Pipeline and opening of two CNG daughter stations capable of dispensing CNG to more than 2,500 vehicles and 50 trucks daily. Ekpo during the opening of two CNG daughter stations capable of dispensing CNG to more than 2,500 vehicles and 50 trucks daily in Kano, on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. He said that the days of those exploiting Nigerian’s by taking advantage of the federal government’s CNG programme to acquire kits, buy CNG, and still charge unsuspecting Nigerians the same as those using petrol will soon be over. According to him, the goal is to flood the country with more CNG stations to meet the current high demand and encourage even more Nigerians, especially commercial drivers, to convert their vehicles. The minister also urged those alleging that the process of obtaining funds for CNG infrastructure expansion from the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund was not transparent and almost impossible. He challenged them to back such claims with evidence, adding that those who have complied with all the requirements have accessed the funds. item.title: Quinn The Corgi Turns Panthers Halftime Into A Viral Dash
item.description: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Quinn, a one-year-old corgi weighing just 25 pounds, broke free from her handlers during halftime at Bank of America Stadium on Sunday. The small dog dodged several attempts to catch her before finally being corralled near the 40-yard line, according to wtvcfox. While the Denver Broncos secured a 26-21 victory over the Carolina Panthers, the real highlight of the game belonged to the short-legged pup who turned a planned race into a chaotic dash. The 2026 Carolina Cup Chaos The event was officially dubbed the 2026 Carolina Cup and featured a dozen adorable competitors including Winnie, Sausage, Daisy, Colorado, and Ollie. Although HITC reports that Ollie won the race, Quinn stole the show by dashing around the field after the event. Quinn appeared destined for the end zone before handlers managed to bring her under control. The hilarious video of the escape made the NFL Red Zone channel, spreading the moment far beyond the stadium. Beforehand, even the Panthers players got involved by offering their predictions for the race. How Quinn Trained for the Dash Quinn Gilgan is short-legged, even for a corgi, but she has been training for moments like this. Durden told WRAL that they take Quinn out to a field every day and make her run, and she would run straight into Gilgan’s arms. Even Durden struggled to catch Quinn on the football field during practice. The dog’s real name is Quinn, though she was referred to as ‘Lennox’ throughout social media memes after Barstool Sports shared a graphic with that wrong name, per HITC. The Charlotte Corgi Club, which organized the event, confirmed her name in a statement. “Go Quinn Go! We had the best time at the Carolina Panthers game today and always love being a part of halftime!” the group said on their Facebook page, according to HITC. A Community Effort on the Field Getting a spot in the race is not guaranteed for every dog owner. Julie Sippy, who founded the Charlotte Corgi Club, told WRAL that corgi owners contribute $15 to a raffle with the goal of obtaining one of the 12 available positions for the halftime race. This year, 137 corgi parents submitted tickets for the chance to be on the field. Proceeds from the event were divided equally between the club and that year’s charity organization. A Facebook group for corgi owners that shares race news and training tips includes Gilgan. The Panthers face the New Orleans Saints next on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 1 p.m. ET in the Caesars Superdome.

item.title: Juste Jocyte’s future with Valkyries uncertain after candid comments to Lithuanian media
item.description: David Gonzales-Imagn Images Juste Jocyte’s future with Valkyries uncertain after candid comments to Lithuanian media appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . While the Golden State Valkyries continue to bask in the glow of the 2026 WNBA Championship, there appear to be some stormy clouds on the offseason horizon regarding the future of their 2025 lottery pick, Juste Jocyte. In her home country of Lithuania, Jocyte spoke candidly to the European media about her mixed feelings regarding her rookie season with Golden State this past year, a season in which she won a championship and endeared herself to the Valkyries’ fanbase and local community, but also did not see much playing time in the process. item.title: ‘No One Wants This’: NCAAF Playoff Expands To 24 Teams, Kills SEC Title Game
item.description: Georgia quarterback Stetson Bennett (13) raises the SEC Championship MVP trophy after the SEC Championship NCAA college football game between LSU and Georgia in Atlanta, on Saturday, Dec. 3, 2022. Georgia won 50-30. News Joshua L Jones Starting in 2027, the College Football Playoff will expand to 24 teams, while the SEC Championship Game will be eliminated. ESPN and the playoff committee finalized a five-year deal valued at nearly $1.7 billion , triggering this huge change. ESPN is set to pay an additional $345 million per year for this new larger format. On Nov. 9, the College Football Playoff Management Committee unanimously approved expansion to 24 teams beginning with the 2027–28 season. The CFP also announced a new media-rights agreement with ESPN, which will carry the expanded playoff through the 2031–32 season. Fans do not appear excited about the changes, as CFP executive director Rich Clark noted earlier this week , “We’re aware of the fan sentiment and that many fans aren’t in favor of expansion. It was considered, but ultimately, we just need to make a spectacular playoff.” Regular Season Games Still Count Some people worry that a bigger bracket means the regular season loses its sting. Earlier this season, Will Stein, the head coach at Kentucky, even spoke about the idea that regular season games might no longer matter. “I think that’s a really lame take, to be honest,” he said Tuesday at his weekly news conference . “As far as I know, every game in college football is still going to matter. … So (the playoff) definitely needed to expand.” Stein made it clear that fans should not dismiss the importance of every Saturday. The new format gives programs like Kentucky a better shot at reaching the national stage and hosting a major game in Lexington. While some fans in Big Blue Nation are unhappy about losing the conference title game, the expanded field offers more teams a path to a national championship. Projected Rankings Shift After Week 10 As the future changes, the current rankings are also likely to be shaken up after Week 10. Georgia is set to take over as the No. 1 team in the second College Football Playoff rankings. Utah will probably move to No. 2 after a big rivalry win against Brigham Young. A pair of two-loss SEC teams could also climb into the top four spots soon. Since Notre Dame defeated Miami, the selection committee is expected to respect that result by ranking the Hurricanes below the Fighting Irish. For the Irish, that would require a big leap from last week’s No. 11 ranking. Following their win over LSU, Alabama has grounds to move up two spots to No. 3, while Texas might pass Indiana after winning at Missouri. Do not expect Ohio State near the top this week; the Buckeyes will stay in the Top 25 but likely land near No. 20 after a poor showing in a home loss to Oregon. item.title: The 1 trade Browns must make in final week before 2026 NFL trade deadline
item.description: The 1 trade Browns must make in final week before 2026 NFL trade deadline appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Cleveland Browns have discovered that fourth-quarter magic cannot compensate for a broken offensive line. Todd Monken’s team has repeatedly found ways to win close games. However, its inability to protect the quarterback is becoming an increasingly dangerous weakness. With 38 sacks allowed through nine games, Cleveland leads the NFL in a category no contender wants to own. The solution may not be another expensive offensive tackle. Instead, general manager Andrew Berry should pursue a more attainable reinforcement: Los Angeles Chargers tight end Charlie Kolar. A reunion with Monken could give the Browns the blocking help they desperately need . Growing protection crisis Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images Through the first nine weeks of 2026, Monken’s debut season in Cleveland has resembled an exhilarating yet harrowing ride. The Browns recovered from an opening blowout in Jacksonville and built a 5-2 record through several dramatic finishes. Andre Szmyt’s clutch kicking and Deshaun Watson’s late-game execution helped Cleveland repeatedly escape tight contests. However, that resilience has masked an escalating crisis in the trenches. The problem became impossible to ignore in a humiliating Week 8 defeat in Pittsburgh. Watson was sacked eight times before entering concussion protocol. Shedeur Sanders took over against New Orleans in Week 9 and showed considerable poise. He threw for 297 yards and two touchdowns. However, the Browns still lost in overtime . Cleveland is now 5-4 . Its ability to protect whoever starts at quarterback could determine whether its playoff ambitions survive. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Crying out for help The cold reality of the trade market is that quality offensive tackles rarely become available in November. Contending teams protect their bookend blockers. Rebuilding franchises understandably demand substantial draft compensation for established starters. Berry cannot simply expect to find a plug-and-play tackle without surrendering valuable future assets. Of course, doing nothing is not an acceptable alternative. Watson has already absorbed a brutal amount of punishment. Sanders was sacked five times against New Orleans despite his mobility. Cleveland also struggled to establish its ground game. They have managed just 95 rushing yards on 34 attempts against the Saints. That combination makes life unnecessarily difficult for any quarterback operating Monken’s offense. The Browns need additional protection without sacrificing their ability to attack downfield. One practical answer is adding a battle-tested inline tight end. He can align beside vulnerable tackles, chip edge rushers, and help establish the perimeter in the running game. That is where Kolar becomes particularly interesting. item.title: Brian Flores’ future with Vikings in serious danger after MNF loss to Bills
item.description: Brian Flores is arguably the best defensive coordinator in the NFL right now. Monday night’s loss to Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills offered another reminder of just how important he has been to the Minnesota Vikings ’ success this season. As has been the case all season, Flores’ defense gave the Vikings several opportunities to win. However, the team’s offense again failed to hold their end of the bargain. With the Vikings on a losing skid, the imbalance in offense and defense is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore, and Minnesota could soon face a difficult decision. MORE: Joe Buck, Troy Aikman able to laugh again thanks to Carson Wentz’s MNF performance Brian Flores’ defense was Vikings’ only positive against Bills Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores. Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Credit: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Minnesota’s 23-6 defeat against Buffalo was another frustrating example of an offense wasting a strong defensive performance. Flores’ unit intercepted Josh Allen once, recorded four sacks and limited the Bills to 339 total yards on Monday. The Bills also averaged just 4.3 yards per play. Meanwhile, Carson Wentz completed just eight of 25 passes for 81 yards. He threw two interceptions and lost a fumble as the Vikings managed only 178 total yards. Just a ridiculous play from Byron Murphy to track down the end zone INT BUFvsMIN on ESPN⁰Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/dISfsc5sQL — NFL (@NFL) November 10, 2026 Despite entering Week 9 with the NFL’s best scoring defense at 13.3 points allowed per game, Minnesota couldn’t get enough support that now ranks as the sixth-worst in the league after Monday. MORE: Vikings trade rumor details deadline plans at quarterback, two potential options Brian Flores could become a major name in the next coaching carousel While finding solutions to the problems at quarterback remains the immediate priority, the Vikings’ biggest concern might be keeping Flores beyond this season. The defensive coordinator has attracted head coaching interest for multiple years, interviewing with the Baltimore Ravens and Pittsburgh Steelers in January 2026. He eventually signed a contract extension with Minnesota on Jan. 21. However, with another coaching cycle approaching in 2027, Flores’ work this season will draw interest from several teams, and the Vikings know too well that losing him would mean replacing an important part of their identity. Head coach Kevin O’Connell has another compelling reason to keep his defensive coordinator around. But how the Vikings finish the season could play a huge part in whether Flores decides to stay or leave. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: World Cup finalists England still feel short of best
item.description: Rob Hawkins laughed when asked by BBC Sport whether he had been practising his dives. The question was prompted by some spectacular athleticism as he scored five tries to help England crush Australia 86-18 in Tuesday's Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup semi-final in Wollongong, Australia. "It's just off-the-cuff stuff when needed," he said. "Some of the kicks were cautious!" The man who had provided many of those kicks, Nathan Collins, was sitting beside him. He did not disagree. "He makes my bad kicks look good!" Collins said. "It is great to have him there to sweep up. He's great to play with and against." England have reason to be in good spirits as they prepare for a fifth successive World Cup final, the fourth in a row against great rivals France. They are looking to defend the title they won on home ground four years ago, a narrow 28-24 victory in Manchester . All of the three previous finals between the two teams have been tight: France won 42-40 in Gillingham in 2013, and 38-34 in Perpignan in 2017. England seemed to set themselves up perfectly for Friday's final, scoring 15 tries against Australia. Hawkins' five scores, plus five conversions, took his personal points tally to 30 points. His best try, and the standout from the whole game, was the third one - a long-range punt from England seemed to be a shot to nothing, but not where Hawkins was concerned. He chased it down and, millimetres away from the dead-ball line, managed to grab the ball and get it down under huge pressure from Adam Tannock, who he had outpaced. Yet Hawkins thought his and England's performances were far from perfect. "Wouldn't say we are 10 out of 10 yet, there are still good a good few things to look at," he said. "Today was a six or seven. Hopefully the best is to come on Friday. "Today was satisfying but not easy. We had the crowd to fight and a ruthless Australian team. But we are happy with the result." England will now reset for their latest showdown with France, which will kick off at 08:45 GMT on Friday at WIN Entertainment Centre. England thrash Australia to reach Wheelchair RL World Cup final How Hawkins overcame illness to star for England Chair skills, quick brain - how O'Neill adapted to wheelchair rugby league 'It has given me a lease of life' Nathan Collins is one of five members of the England squad who played in the 2022 World Cup final [Getty Images] Collins said England will need to repeat their dominant performance against Australia, and more, to beat the only other nation ever to win the world title. "We've got to do what we did today, stick to the process Tom [Coyd, the England coach] has put in front of us," he said. "It looks like a good game, but there is still plenty to do. "We are used to big games, league titles and Challenge Cups. This is a step up from that, so we go again." item.title: Should Washington Commanders move Stefon Diggs at NFL trade deadline?
item.description: On Monday, Sean McVay indicated that Puka Nucua is likely to be placed on injured reserve following multiple sprains to the ligaments in his knee, and with Davante Adams still on IR, the 5-4 L.A. Rams may now be motivated buyers for a wide receiver before Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. One of their possible trade targets could be Washington Commanders wide receiver Stefon Diggs. The Rams are looking to win now, but one of their biggest stumbling blocks could be a lack of cap space to acquire a player at the deadline. There are, however, plenty of playoff contenders who need a receiver. Would the Commanders be willing to part with a DMV native they signed during training camp? And at what cost? Diggs is a proven, valuable commodity to the right team. According to Spotrac , since much of Diggs’ contract is tied to incentives, the team acquiring the Commanders wide receiver would only take on a $2.9 million cap hit. Diggs’ skill set and experience also make him a viable replacement for what Sean McVay will be missing while Nucua recovers from injury. Meanwhile, Diggs wasn’t used much early in Sunday’s game and ended up with three receptions on the day. His final catch, with under a minute left, got the Commanders within striking distance of beating the Rams and demonstrated his play-making ability but also caused some frustration for head coach Dan Quinn. In an interview with WUSA9, Quinn expressed how he would have liked Diggs to finish the play differently. Sometimes five extra yards can cost you more than they’re worth. Dan Quinn explained why he wanted Stefon Diggs to get out of bounds on the Commanders’ final drive instead of fighting for extra yards. Quinn breaks down Washington’s final seconds against the Rams. pic.twitter.com/jgunnTWXFz — Marshall Kramsky (@marshallkramsky) November 9, 2026 Diggs has been Washington’s most productive wide receiver this year, with 30 receptions for 303 receiving yards and 5 TDs, but also five drops, which have cost the team at various times during the season. The mercurial wide receiver also incurred a costly unsportsmanlike conduct penalty in Week 1 versus the Philadelphia Eagles. While the Commanders have significant losses of their own at the wide receiver position, at 2-5-1, their playoff hopes hang on the slim possibility they can overtake the Giants and Cowboys to win their division. A recent article floated Diggs’ trade value as a 2027 fourth-round selection, but that seems a bit steep for a soon to be 33-year-old wide receiver with only half the regular season left. The most likely compensation for any offer would be a 5th or 6th round selection. While Stefon Diggs still provides a proven receiving threat and veteran presence, Adam Peters may have to weigh the team’s current season outlook against the possibility adding more draft capital if the LA Rams or another team comes calling before today’s deadline. item.title: Is Tony Romo Set to Replace Troy Aikman at ESPN After Surprise ‘MNF’ Appearance?
item.description: Tony Romo and Troy Aikman - Tony Romo and Troy Aikman (Gail Schulman/CBS and Stacy Revere; Getty Images) NFL fans were in for a surprise on Monday night when former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo made his return to TV, appearing on Pat McAfee ’s Monday Night Football alternate broadcast on ESPN2 during the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings game. The cameo marked Romo’s first media appearance in over three months following his July 23 arrest for operating while intoxicated in Wisconsin, an incident that resulted in CBS Sports placing him on indefinite leave and the two parties eventually parting ways in October with a settlement on his remaining contract. Romo appeared early in the second quarter as McAfee introduced him as the show’s “quarterback expert.” “I’m doing good and I’m sorry Dan [Orlovsky] that they gave me the quarterback specialist here, but you know that I think you’re a great quarterback guru,” Romo said on the segment. McAfee praised the former analyst during the segment, telling him, “We all miss you.” LADIES AND GENTLEMEN.. item.title: Frank Kennedy’s Q School DQ Sparks Debate On Green Damage
item.description: Stephen Lew-USA TODAY Sports Frank Kennedy, a 21-year-old English pro, found out the hard way on Monday that the DP World Tour will not tolerate damage to the putting surface. After allegedly removing a one-foot divot from the 11th green at Infinitum Golf in Spain, officials disqualified him from the Final Stage of Qualifying School. Kennedy claims the damage was not intentional. He told the world on Instagram that he missed a birdie putt and swung his club in frustration, noting that the putter “accidentally caught the surface.” He insists he did not mean to hurt the green and that his playing partner helped fix it right away. “I am hugely disappointed to have been disqualified …” Kennedy wrote, according to a report . He added that reports claiming he damaged the course on purpose are “wholly incorrect.” The young golfer admitted he should have called a referee to check the repair before moving on, but he argues that accidental contact should not cost him his entire tournament. The Rules Do Not Care About Feelings While Kennedy says he learned a lesson, the rules of golf are strict about who fixes what and when. The DP World Tour confirmed to Monday Q Info that the disqualification was necessary because the damage was deemed deliberate. The top 15 players and ties will earn DPWT cards for 2027, a prize Kennedy now misses. If players can damage greens and claim it was an accident without consequence, the rules become meaningless. The tournament officials saw a player swing a club and hit the green, causing a visible divot. They decided that the act was egregious enough to end his run. Kennedy stated he would respect the outcome of a review, but the initial ruling stands firm. Accidents Happen, But Consequences Remain Kennedy shot a 69 in the fourth round and was in position to make the cut before the DQ. Even if the damage was not meant to be malicious, the result was the same: a ruined putting surface and a disqualified player. After posting a 69 in the fourth round, Kennedy tied for the final spot in the top 60 to play the last two rounds. His DQ shifted the cut line from 12 under to 11 under, causing seven players who would have been eliminated to survive instead. DPWT cards for 2027 will be awarded to the top 15 players and ties.

item.title: Texans’ Derek Stingley Details Why CJ Stroud is Better Than Any Other NFL QB
item.description: The Houston Texans are picking up steam after a brutal start to their 2026 NFL campaign. Thanks in large part to the great play under center by quarterback CJ Stroud , Houston has seemingly started to turn things around. The Texans lost their first four games of the season but have since won three of four outings, including a 44-22 demolition of the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood in Week 9. For Houston defensive back Derek Stingley Jr., Stroud is already the No. 1 signal-caller in the league based on his objective observation. “I think he’s the best in the league,” Stingley said of Stroud, via Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston (h/t Houston Stressans ). “I’m not saying that just because I’m on his team. He actually the best in the league. Whether he got time to throw, whether he don’t, he gonna make a play. We seen it in practice. It’s just crazy.” Texans QB Stroud Has Been Steady in 2026 Aug 28, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; A detail view of a Houston Texans helmet before the game against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images With Stroud running the show for the offense on the field, the Texans are in the top 10 in the league thus far in scoring offense with 26.1 points per game and 11th overall with 356.5 total yards per outing. If the passing game is only being complemented by a much more effective rushing attack, it would be a better story for Houston. Through nine weeks, the Texans are only rushing 87.1 yards per game, so it has been mostly Stroud carrying Houston’s offense. So far this season, the 25-year-old Stroud has passed for 2,251 yards and 16 touchdowns. He has been so good at avoiding interceptions, with only two to his name, while completing 64.2 percent of his passes. item.title: Tresoldi on Bayern shortlist despite Kane extension
item.description: Tresoldi on Bayern shortlist despite Kane extension Bayern Munich have previously been mentioned among the top clubs keeping an eye on Club Brugge and Germany U21 forward Nicolò Tresoldi. According to local outlet TZ, the German champions continue to have the 22-year-old on their shortlist despite recently tying Harry Kane down to a new contract until 2029, as they consider adding a second “weapon” to their squad up front. item.title: Barcelona star De Jong open to Netherlands captaincy: ‘It would be an honour’
item.description: Barcelona star De Jong open to Netherlands captaincy: ‘It would be an honour’ After an injury-laden summer, Frenkie de Jong will once again return to Dutch colours this week as we enter the second international break of the season. The Barcelona midfielder is coming on the back of a stellar cameo against Atletico Madrid, where he was able to calm the game and help his team secure a 2-1 victory. Now back in the Netherlands camp under the new but familiar manager, Xavi Hernandez, Frenkie is tipped to become the team captain in the absence of Virgil van Dijk. Frenkie open to captaincy De Jong addressed the media over the possibility of becoming a captain, confirming that the final decision is up to Xavi. De Jong played a key role in Barcelona’s win over Atletico Madrid. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) But the Barcelona midfielder stated he would be more than happy to become the captain of the national team, in the absence of van Dijk. “It depends on the coach to announce it, but it is certainly possible. I’m not very talkative. Virgil is always heard above others, he is our true leader, also verbally. “When I wear the armband, I can set an example for others with my behaviour and professionalism,” he said (h/t SPORT ). De Jong added that his captaincy style could be a mix of both Lionel Messi and van Dijk, as he is not really a vocal leader on the pitch. “I also experienced having Messi as captain. He never raised his voice and was the undisputed boss. Let’s say that, with the armband, I would be somewhere between Messi and Virgil. It would be a great honour if it happened this week ,” he added. De Jong on Xavi’s methods Frenkie has worked with Xavi in the past. (Photo by Catherine Ivill/Getty Images) De Jong went on to talk about Xavi’s adaptation and tactical setup in the Netherlands team, having previously worked with the Spaniard at Barcelona. “It is very clear in their approach and what they want to see. During the first international break I already observed some patterns in the construction of the game that are characteristic of it. The fact that I was also a midfielder is especially pleasant .” The Barcelona midfielder is also open to the possibility of appearing alongside Borussia Dortmund Joey Veerman. “I agree with the coach in which good footballers can always play together. Joey is tactically solid, technically good and has a great vision of play. There are a lot of midfielders in the national team that I can play with ,” he said. Finally, the Dutchman offered an update on his fitness, having recently returned from a long injury layoff. “I’m fit, happy and very motivated. I don’t think you’ll learn anything from injuries, but you do want to play football again ,” he concluded.

item.title: NBA Expert Changes His Tune on Celtics' Jaylen Brown-Paul George Trade
item.description: NBA Expert Changes His Tune on Celtics' Jaylen Brown-Paul George Trade originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Jaylen Brown-Paul George trade is looking like a much better decision for the Boston Celtics . Ahead of Tuesday's matchup between the Celtics and 76ers, The Sporting News' Stephen Noh regraded the offseason's blockbuster trade. Whereas he originally gave the Celtics a C- for the deal, Noh now gives them an A. "George has also taken on a good chunk of the offensive load for Boston," wrote Noh . "While he's no longer an elite driver, he draws a ton of defensive attention from his shooting. The Celtics have him flying off screens, getting him clean looks or advantages going downhill. "What also makes this trade even better for Boston is how good those future picks are looking. At the time, it wasn't immediately obvious how bad the Clippers would be in 2028 when the Celtics received the option to swap first-rounders with them. "Now, after trading away Kawhi Leonard and getting hit with multiple penalties by Adam Silver, it's almost a surefire bet that the Clippers will be among the worst teams in the league. Boston should have the best odds possible for a top pick in that deep draft." MORE: How Paul George, Jaylen Brown Have Performed Since Trade Noh also gave the 76ers an A for the deal, calling it a "win-win" for both teams. George has gotten off to an excellent start in Boston. Through nine games, he's averaging 20.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, 4.1 assists and 2.3 steals per game while shooting a career-best 42.5 percent from 3-point range. He's played a big role in Boston's 8-2 start, which has the Celtics sitting half a game behind the 76ers for first place in the Eastern Conference. The question, of course, is whether George can keep this up. George played only 78 games over two seasons with the Philadelphia 76ers. He's played 60-plus games only once over the last seven seasons, making his durability a legitimate concern at 36. Still, the Celtics didn't just get George in the trade. They also acquired draft compensation, including a convoluted 2028 first-round pick involving the Clippers that could become particularly valuable . George's strong start has already made the trade look better for the Celtics. If the Clippers continue to struggle, it could look even better down the road.
