item.title: 3 Liverpool players who should get new contracts soon — and 2 who shouldn't
item.description: Virgil van Dijk and Alisson Becker after Liverpool vs Villarreal in the Champions League. -Credit:Ed Sykes/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images Virgil van Dijk and Alisson Becker after Liverpool vs Villarreal in the Champions League. -Credit:Ed Sykes/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images Following Alisson Becker's impressive display against Crystal Palace, the goalkeeper spoke candidly about his contract situation. His "will", he said, is to remain at the club beyond the end of the season. As it stands, Alisson's Liverpool contract is due to expire at that point. Having attracted transfer interest from Juventus during the summer, there was a prevailing belief that he might be tempted by a fresh challenge. That doesn't appear to be the case, however: it couldn't be more apparent that the 34 year old and his family are content where they are. "Yes, in my mind," Alisson told reporters at Selhurst Park when asked if he wants to extend his deal. "I'm focused on playing every game, but in my mind I'm happy to stay. "You know, that depends on a lot of aspects and different situations. But my will is to stay. I'm still hungry for titles and for delivering good performances. I still want to play at the top level for as long as I can. So that's my thinking on that.", reports Liverpool.com . Given that Alisson continues to perform at a high level, that he brings such vast experience, and that quality goalkeepers who meet Liverpool's demanding requirements are so difficult to find, extending his contract appears to be a straightforward decision. However, including the Brazilian shot-stopper, five senior Liverpool players are currently set to see their contracts expire at the same time, meaning the club's decision-making process is far from over. Like Alisson, Virgil van Dijk is well into his 30s and now in the latter stages of his career, but the Liverpool captain falls into the same category. He continues to perform at a high level and remains a significant presence in the locker room. Van Dijk is currently helping mentor Jeremy Jacquet, and with Giovanni Leoni having been sidelined through injury for such an extended period, there isn't as clear a candidate to assume his minutes as there might have been had his transfer proceeded as planned. Retaining Van Dijk, should he be open to signing a one-year extension, would seem to be a sensible decision. Meanwhile, another defender in Joe Gomez is scheduled to be out of contract next summer. The long-serving, versatile star hasn't been a regular for quite some time, but his importance is evident too. Beyond being a homegrown player, he can fill any defensive position. Should he be content to stay as a squad option, it would be the correct decision to retain him. Kostas Tsimikas, however, represents a different scenario. Having returned from a loan spell at AS Roma, he has delivered inconsistent performances to date, and it would be beneficial to have a superior player competing with Milos Kerkez for minutes. Even

item.title: Harrison Armstrong passes Stones and Barkley in Everton's teen PL starts list
item.description: Harrison Armstrong during Everton's 3-1 win over Coventry City -Credit:Reach Publishing Services Limited Harrison Armstrong during Everton's 3-1 win over Coventry City Harrison Armstrong has now surpassed John Stones and Ross Barkley in terms of Premier League starts for Everton as a teenager (16), though I recently stumbled across a statistic online revealing I actually top that list with 61, a full 21 ahead of Wayne Rooney in second place. It genuinely caught me off guard, as it's something I was completely unaware of. I can't help but wonder, had I been best mates with Walter Smith and he hadn't brought in three other left-backs in David Unsworth, Alessandro Pistone and Gary Naysmith, just how high those numbers could have climbed. That's one of the genuine upsides of social media — you discover things about yourself you never knew. It was a welcome little positive and gratifying to see my name at the summit of that list, particularly given the caliber of players below me who went on to forge outstanding careers. Armstrong is getting his chance. I don't believe Harrison will be taken aback, but he'll certainly appreciate the volume of playing time he's receiving and the level of confidence David Moyes is placing in him. At the beginning of the season, there was genuine uncertainty over whether he'd head out on loan again. Evertonians were eager to see more of him, but ultimately it came down to his dedication throughout pre-season, his work in training, and the quality he's consistently demonstrated, reports the Liverpool Echo . Performing well every single week isn't realistic, and that's something every young player experiences. I recall numerous matches where I walked off the field thinking I couldn't remember doing anything particularly good or bad. Getting on the ball is the key priority. Harrison operates in the engine room, giving him every opportunity to make that happen. Playing at left-back limited my own ability to get on the ball as much as I would have preferred. He has demonstrated real leadership qualities at a young age. That booking he received for what I considered an outstanding tackle against Chelsea galvanized the crowd and the entire Everton squad — he was stepping up and taking responsibility. Harrison has the tools in his arsenal, and with each additional game comes greater experience, greater knowledge, and continued development. You absorb lessons from the best players around you in the locker room and incorporate that into your own game. This is a tremendous moment for the academy. We've endured years of frustration watching talented players denied their shot, and in some cases, we've allowed them to leave. Seeing one of our brightest prospects finally given his opportunity — and seizing it — is exactly what this club needed.

item.title: Stanford's century-long AI study admits it's already out of date
item.description: Twelve years into Stanford's 100-year study of artificial intelligence, the project's third report raises more questions than it answers. The 2026 AI100 Study Panel report acknowledges its limitations in its twelfth takeaway: "This report will be out of date by the time you read it." But it's nonetheless a worthwhile exercise for those who haven't been paying close attention to the development of machine learning over the past few years and for policymakers who may benefit from a review of AI's metastatic growth. "The last five years constitute a watershed moment in the history of AI," said Professor Sheila McIlraith, chair of the AI100 Standing Committee, in a statement. " This report examines what led to the extraordinary capabilities of today's AI systems, and how they are reshaping society. As we look ahead, we anticipate continued increase in AI capabilities alongside transformative advances in science and medicine. "Rapid change will challenge governments and industry to support and safeguard our people, our institutions, and our critical infrastructure. Both the benefits and the risks of AI technologies require the same clear-eyed scrutiny." Established in 2014, the One Hundred Year Study on Artificial Intelligence (AI100) is overseen by a Standing Committee of AI experts and administered by Stanford's Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (HAI). It's charged with producing reports every five years, the first of which debuted in 2016. The 2026 report's other key points highlight the transformation brought about by increasingly capable machine learning software. It identifies scaling as the engine of AI's advance, but also points to the growing cost and difficulty of obtaining training data as constraints on further progress. The report likens AI's disruptive potential to that of the World Wide Web – without dwelling on the irony that the web itself is among the things being disrupted. It points to creative industries, computer programming, and mathematics as fields once deemed beyond the reach of automation that are now being upended. Science, the report says, is being transformed by AI as it accelerates research timelines and opens up novel challenges. At the same time, the report cautions that "we will need to understand how AI-mediated information environments reshape collective cognition and moral behavior." The recent retraction of some 1,400 scholarly papers for failure to meet academic standards highlights the urgency of that message. Then there's the AI investment boom and "fears of a financial bubble, " which won't be assuaged by recent NASDAQ volatility and revelations about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with an alleged intelligence operative for China. Concerns about the concentration of frontier AI development, the pressure AI puts on cybersecurity, and the active use of AI for military applications are also noted in the report. So too are worries about what AI-generated media does to trust. Item nine on

item.title: See the first images from the new ZWO Seestar S30 Plus — a smart telescope aimed at beginners
item.description: null As rival makers announce increasingly ambitious smart telescopes , ZWO has taken a different approach. Its new Seestar S30 Plus launches today and will be available online from Seestar’s website and Amazon, just in time for Christmas. Better still, we’ve been using it for a month and can bring you a first look. Announced a few months after the flagship Seestar S50 Pro and replacing the now-discontinued Seestar S30 , the new Seestar S30 Plus retains its 30mm aperture and compact chassis, but upgrades to four-element apochromatic optics with extra-low dispersion (ED) glass and two 3.7-megapixel cameras. The ZWO Seestar S30 Plus is a new sub-$500 smart telescope with upgraded optics and dual 3.7MP cameras. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) Both produce 1,440 x 2,560-pixel images, while a much-improved 43.5-degree wide-angle camera can capture the Milky Way , constellations , star trails and nightscapes. Built-in filters, a mosaic mode and equatorial (EQ) tracking add considerable deep-sky astrophotography potential. For a telescope weighing just 3.64 lbs (1.65 kg), it’s impressive. It easily fits into a camera bag and could happily live on a bookshelf. The Seestar S30 Plus weighs just 3.64 lbs (1.65 kg) and fits in a camera bag easily. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) I’ve already photographed the Andromeda Galaxy (M31) , the Pleiades (M45) , the Dumbbell Nebula (M27) and the North America Nebula (NGC 7000). The results are excellent for such a small instrument, especially when imaging nebulas with its built-in dual-band filter, which helps reduce light pollution. The Seestar app adds new in-app post-processing options, so you don’t have to mess around with any of that — though you can also export everything as lossless FITS files. The S30 Plus also includes a magnetic solar filter, enabling you to indulge in solar photography safely. The North America Nebula (NGC 7000), the Pleiades (M45) and a star trail imaged using the Seestar S30 Plus. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) With Dwarflab’s $1,299 Draco (3.5-inch/90mm aperture) recently landed in stores and Vaonis’ own $4,990 Atlas (3.1-inch/80mm aperture) not available until 2027, ZWO’s decision to offer an upgraded entry-level smart telescope that buyers can get their hands on right now looks particularly smart. The Andromeda Galaxy (M31) photographed using the Seestar S30 Plus. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) With ZWO's pattern of delivering cheaper smart telescopes without sacrificing on quality, the Seestar S30 Plus could be one of Christmas 2026’s best gifts for anyone interested in astronomy — and maybe that’s the point of it. Either way, first impressions are good. A full review is coming tomorrow, so check back at Space.com to find out our full thoughts and testing.

item.title: Meet only two countries to have won both men’s, women’s U-20 World Cups
item.description: Germany and Spain are the only two countries to have won both the FIFA U-20 Men’s World Cup and the FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup. The two European nations have achieved the feat by winning titles in both competitions, which showcase some of the world’s best emerging football talents. Germany became the first to accomplish the double, with its men’s team, then competing as West Germany, winning the U-20 World Cup in 1981. The country’s women’s team subsequently claimed the U-20 Women’s World Cup in 2004, 2010 and 2014, taking its tally to three titles in the competition. Spain also joined the exclusive list after winning the men’s U-20 World Cup in 1999, when the tournament was hosted by Nigeria. The Spanish men’s team defeated Japan 4-0 in the final in Lagos to secure its first title. More than two decades later, Spain’s women’s team won its maiden U-20 Women’s World Cup in 2022, defeating Japan 3-1 in the final in Costa Rica. Spain added a second women’s title in 2026, further strengthening its record across both competitions. The achievement places Germany and Spain in a select group of countries that have conquered both sides of FIFA’s U-20 World Cup competitions. item.title: A science fiction novel has finally won the Booker prize. It’s about time
item.description: M. John Harrison is considered the first bona fide science fiction author to win the Booker prize Kirsty Wigglesworth/AP/Alamy Back in June, our science fiction columnist Emily H. Wilson made a bold claim : M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything was not only “the best science-fiction book of the year so far”, but also a “wholly original… work of genius”. Not only has Emily been proved right, but perhaps she didn’t go quite far enough. This story of an alien invasion won the Booker prize last night, making it – in the Booker judges’ opinion, at least – not just the best science fiction book of the year so far, but the best novel in any genre of the year. Read more These two new sci-fi novels really impressed us It’s about time. Back in 2009, the great Kim Stanley Robinson – another writer of genius, in my opinion – wrote a piece for New Scientist in which he argued that “three or four of the last 10 Booker prizes should have gone to science fiction novels the juries hadn’t read”. With remarkable prescience, Robinson even tipped Harrison’s Signs of Life as one of those books. Advertisement There has been a long-running reluctance in the literary world to allow science fiction (often abbreviated to SF) into the starry ranks of so-called “literary” fiction. As Harrison himself told the BBC’s Front Row last month, he has “been working for 40 to 50 years to shift the balance, both as a novelist and as a critic… Why shouldn’t a well written SF be considered to be literary fiction?”. His win is being trumpeted today as the first time a science fiction novel has won the Booker prize. I’d quibble a little with that – how about Margaret Atwood’s The Testaments , the sequel to The Handmaid’s Tale , set in a dystopian version of the US, which was 2019’s winner? She’d likely quibble with me in return: Atwood has a lot to say about the difference between science fiction and speculative fiction, defining her Gilead stories firmly as the latter. Free newsletter Sign up to Book Club Sign up to newsletter But this very unwillingness to define a novel as science fiction speaks to that long-running literary snobbery. As the late, great Ursula K. Le Guin put it, reviewing Atwood’s The Year of the Flood back in 2009: “She doesn’t want the literary bigots to shove her into the literary ghetto.” Whether or not Harrison is the first science fiction author to win the Booker, it’s definitely the case that, as Booker Prize Foundation chief executive Gaby Wood put it in the prize announcement: “Many past Booker Prize authors have borrowed facets of science fiction in their work, but M. John Harrison is the first Booker winner to have emerged from the bona fide SF world.” And this means, I hope, that our days of looking down on science fiction are over. Harrison’s brilliant book tells the story of Phillip Tennent, a beachcomber who lives with his grandmother on the Kent coast, in the wake of the invasion of mysterious shapeshifting entities called the iGhetti. item.title: Obi will run to Cameroon if confronted with burdens of presidency – Wike
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has accused the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, of lacking the capacity to tackle the myriads of Nigeria’s challenges but would instead flee to Cameroon if handed the responsibilities of the presidency. Wike spoke on Tuesday at the Abaji Area Council Rainbow Coalition and Stakeholders’ Meeting in Abuja, where he urged FCT residents to back President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027. He said Obi would run away from the country’s problems instead of tackling them headlong, unlike Tinubu, whom he praised for taking difficult decisions. According to the minister, Nigeria needs a president who can confront hard situations and not abandon the country when challenges arise. He argued that the presidency is not a position for political theatrics or public relations but one that demands courage, capacity and the willingness to take responsibility. Wike asked the Abaji leaders to prove their support for Tinubu at the polls. He warned political leaders against making promises they cannot fulfil and said he would judge them by their ability to deliver their wards for the President in 2027. “Let me repeat what I said yesterday. To the people of Abaji, through their chairman, councillors and leaders, you come from different wards. You have told me you will vote for Tinubu. I have no problem with that. I want to see it,” he said. He specifically charged the Abaji Area Council chairman and other leaders to secure victory for Tinubu in their wards, stressing that leadership must be shown through electoral results. The minister said the FCT must not only match Rivers State in electoral performance but surpass it, adding that he was ready to apply the same political mobilisation strategy in Abuja. “Nobody is competing with Rivers. I don’t know what you all think. The only people who are going to compete with Rivers are the FCT. Whatever I will do there, I will do it here. So make sure you beat Rivers,” Wike said. Wike also cautioned residents against repeating what he described as the mistake of the 2023 elections, when they allegedly voted for candidates who did not keep in touch with their constituents after winning. “You went and elected somebody you don’t know. Is it not correct? Have you seen the person again? Has he come to address you? Has he asked you what your problems are? Has he moved anything that will affect the interest of the FCT?” he asked. The minister disclosed that he would meet FCT youths on Wednesday to discuss political mobilisation and other issues affecting their participation in the forthcoming elections. He assured stakeholders that the resources and arrangements for the electioneering campaign were being put in place and expressed confidence in the readiness of the Rainbow Coalition to mobilise support for Tinubu. Wike also reiterated his determination to have the electricity challenge in Abaji addressed befo

item.title: Ogun Gov Poll: PDP candidate’s name not in party’s register, INEC tells court
item.description: … as LP chieftain alleges plot to compromise judge By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has explained to the Federal High Court in Abuja why it excluded Ogun State PDP candidate Mr Ladi Adebutu from its list of candidates cleared for the 2027 general elections. In a counter-affidavit deposed to by Mr Mustapha Mohammed, a Chief Program Analyst in its Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Department, the Commission told the court that Adebutu’s name was not found in the register of members the PDP earlier submitted to it. It told the court that it found only the name of the PDP’s deputy governorship candidate in the state, Kolapo Lateefat Oyeyemi, in the register. INEC’s counter-affidavit was in opposition to a suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/2573/2026, which the PDP and its Ogun State governorship candidate, Adebutu, filed against it. While the PDP is the 1st plaintiff in the matter, Adebutu is listed as the 2nd plaintiff, with INEC named as the sole defendant. It will be recalled that INEC had omitted Adebutu’s name from the final list of 13 candidates cleared to contest the Ogun State governorship election billed for February 6, 2027. Dissatisfied with the action, the PDP approached the court for an order compelling INEC to reverse its decision by recognising Adebutu’s candidacy. However, in the process it filed to challenge the competence of the suit, INEC said it had done due diligence before the final list of candidates for the election was published. According to the deponent, “I know as a fact that before the Governorship Candidates Final List was published, the ICT department conducted a search on the membership register submitted by the 1st plaintiff and during the search, the ICT department found the name of the 1st plaintiff’s candidate fielded as Deputy Governor of Ogun State (Kolapo Lateefat Oyeyemi) in the register but could not find the name of the 2nd plaintiff. “The search was also conducted to find a possible match for the name of the 2nd plaintiff, but no possible match was found in the Ogun State membership register. “That I know as a fact that all the queries conducted on the membership register in the flash drives (PDF/read only) submitted to the defendant by the 1st plaintiff do not contain the name of the 2nd plaintiff. “That the flash drive attached to the plaintiff’s affidavit and further affidavit in support of the Originating Summons was shown to me and I have carefully examined it, and I state that the contents of the flash drive are not the same as those submitted to the defendant. “That the first flash drive submitted by the 1st plaintiff to the defendant on 22 April 2026 had files named Ogun 01-038, while the second flash drive submitted to the defendant had files named Ogun 01-04, with serial numbers of members 1–18,973 and 1–19,308 respectively. “That serial number 1536 on the membership register submitted by the 1st plaintiff to the defendant contains the name of one

item.title: Chrome zero-day whack-a-mole continues as 2026 tally hits 8
item.description: Google has patched its eighth actively exploited Chrome zero-day of 2026, matching its total for the whole of last year with nearly two months still left on the calendar. The latest flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-125350, is a high-severity use-after-free vulnerability in Chrome's XML component. Google confirmed in a security advisory published Monday that attackers are already exploiting the bug, although it hasn't said who's behind the attacks or who might be getting targeted. "Google is aware that an exploit for CVE-2026-125350 exists in the wild," the company said, offering little else about the attacks. The vulnerability was reported anonymously on November 6 and involves a memory management error that occurs when software continues using a pointer to memory that has already been freed. Such bugs can potentially allow attackers to corrupt memory and execute malicious code, although Google hasn't disclosed how this particular flaw is being exploited. Google is keeping further technical details under wraps until enough users have installed the fix, a familiar approach intended to stop other attackers from getting their hands on a working exploit. The patch arrives in Chrome 157.0.8103.50/.51 for Windows and macOS, and 157.0.8103.50 for Linux. The update also addresses eight other security vulnerabilities, including high-severity flaws affecting WebGL, FileSystem, GPU, Compositing, and the V8 JavaScript engine. The release fixes another use-after-free bug in Chrome's XML component, CVE-2026-125346, which was reported by Arni Hardarson of Neonix Security in October, though Google hasn't indicated that this second vulnerability is being exploited. The latest discovery adds to what's becoming a rather long list of Chrome zero-days this year. By June, Google had already patched five actively exploited Chrome zero-days , including flaws in its V8 JavaScript engine, Skia graphics library, and WebGPU implementation. The list has only grown since then, with two more V8 bugs fixed in September and the latest XML vulnerability bringing the total to eight. That puts 2026 level with 2025, when Google also fixed eight Chrome zero-days exploited in the wild. Whether the browser maker can make it through the remaining weeks of the year without adding another to the pile is anyone's guess. Google says the latest update will roll out over the coming days and weeks, but users can check manually by heading to Chrome's Settings menu and selecting About Chrome. With attackers already making use of the vulnerability, it's probably worth doing that sooner rather than waiting for Chrome to get around to it. ®

item.title: Kompany returns to Bayern’s training ground for first time since collapse
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany returned to the club’s training ground on Tuesday for the first time since collapsing last month, beginning a gradual return to work ahead of the Bundesliga match against Cologne on November 20. The 40-year-old was at Bayern’s Säbener Straße complex shortly after 10am, according to German media reports. He worked from his office, spoke with assistant coach Floribert Ngalula and sporting director Christoph Freund, and watched injured players complete a recovery session. His return to the training ground does not mean he has resumed all his duties, as he is expected back in the dugout after the international break. Kompany collapsed on October 23 while watching a training session involving Bayern’s reserve team. He was hospitalised and diagnosed with meningeal irritation, an inflammation affecting the tissue around the brain or spinal cord. He was later discharged to recover at home. Assistant Aaron Danks took charge during Kompany’s absence, overseeing four wins and a 2-2 draw with Borussia Dortmund. Bayern beat Freiburg, Magdeburg, Atlético Madrid and Mainz. Danks said the club had instructed him to keep football discussions away from Kompany while he recovered. “I have clear instructions from Max [Eberl] and Christoph [Freund] not to engage in discussions, first of all, and to keep Vince focused on nothing other than his health and spending time with his family,” he said. “We want him to rest and recover properly so that, when he returns, he is fully fit and can help us in the best possible way. We are being very strict here and keeping football completely out of it.” Kompany’s father, Pierre, had previously described his son’s demanding work routine in an interview with Bild. “He works 18 hours a day most days and, on a typical day, barely sees his children,” he said, adding that Kompany was often at the training ground early and left late. Bayern are scheduled to host Cologne on November 20, when Kompany is expected to return to the touchline. The post Kompany returns to Bayern’s training ground for first time since collapse appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Nnaji vows to end excessive taxation in Enugu
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Enugu State, Chief Uche Nnaji, has said he is contesting the 2027 election to rescue the state from what he described as excessive taxation and its impact on businesses and residents. Nnaji alleged that the high tax burden was forcing businessmen and investors to relocate from the state, adding that Enugu had become one of the most expensive places to do business in the country. He spoke while addressing indigenes of Enugu State resident in Aba, Abia State, under the umbrella of the Enugu State Consultative Forum, Abia State chapter. The former Minister of Science and Technology pledged to revive the state’s economy through industrialisation, job creation and measures to address insecurity and unemployment. He said he had been consulting Enugu indigenes living outside the state to draw their attention to what he described as the challenges facing the state and seek their support ahead of the election. Nnaji expressed concern over what he described as the return of armed robbery in parts of Enugu, attributing the development to unemployment, hunger and economic hardship. He promised to establish industries that would create employment opportunities, reduce poverty and take more than 50,000 youths off the streets. “What is happening in Enugu State is condemnable. Enugu is for all, but today, businessmen and investors are relocating from the state due to excessive taxation. And the state government doesn’t care. “Our people are suffering from excessive taxation, even in the rural areas. Traders in rural communities only open their businesses in the evening when tax officials have left. Government collects N36,000 from traders in the villages, when most of them do not make such an amount annually. “Tax is based on profit, not on shops, as they are doing in Enugu. People are hungry. Armed people now invade homes at midnight to collect phones, computers and food items such as rice, beans and garri. This is something that happened more than 20 years ago,” he said. The PDP candidate also questioned the state’s internally generated revenue (IGR), claiming that it had risen from N26 billion to N406.7 billion. He compared the figure with the revenue generated by Abia and Anambra states, arguing that the high revenue collection raised questions about the state’s taxation policies and their impact on businesses. Nnaji further alleged that Enugu’s debt profile had increased significantly under the current administration, although he did not provide figures to substantiate the claim. He said government should focus on creating wealth and improving the living conditions of residents rather than imposing taxes that could undermine businesses. “We have set up the Enugu State Recovery Committee, with me as chairman. This is why we are visiting Enugu people residing outside the state, telling them about the poor situation of things in their state. “Last week, we were a

item.title: ‘Without storyboards, I feel like I’m in Grand Central station in my underwear’: film’s fightback against AI
item.description: As Hollywood begins to adopt the technology, the professionals in most direct jeopardy are the illustrators mapping out directors’ first visions. They sketch out what could be lost A film industry dominated by AI is a dystopian prospect: stories and dialogue generated by large language models, populated by reincarnated screen icons and uncanny humanoids . That is in the future, but the real-world impact of AI is already directly affecting jobs behind the scenes, as Hollywood’s biggest film-makers begin to adopt the technology. James Cameron – long an advocate for emerging technologies in film-making – is on the board of a gen AI firm , citing his interest in how AI will intersect with CGI; Steven Soderbergh used Meta-powered tech to create animations for his recent documentary about John Lennon ; even Christopher Nolan, while dismissing the idea that AI will replace humans as “nonsense”, conceded that it will create some useful “imaging tools”. The current canary in the coalmine however is the storyboard artist, whose work gen AI appears to have directly in its sights. Storyboard artists are the illustrators who draw the panels of images with notes and diagrams that map out scenes before they are filmed. Storyboards are used to work out how a film will look, and as a blueprint to communicate a director’s vision to cast and crew , and are one of the first steps in bringing a script off the page. Now they appear on the verge of replacement by programmes that use text prompts to create illustrations instead. Even an old-school diehard like Martin Scorsese has got on board; in June he announced a partnership with an AI firm whose text-to-image model he used in the storyboarding process for his next movie. item.title: Ransomware threat blares from Vanderbilt University computers during cyberattack
item.description: Classes at Vanderbilt University are proceeding as scheduled today, although access to most university systems remains restricted following a cyberattack claimed by ransomware group BYOD. Vanderbilt announced on Monday morning that it was dealing with "an active cybersecurity incident," and that the fallout may affect university devices, systems, and cloud-based services. The Nashville-based university initially told students and staff to shut down university devices and disconnect from campus Wi-Fi. It warned them to watch for unexpected prompts, altered files or permissions, unfamiliar applications, and unsolicited authentication requests. Campus computers reportedly began playing an audio threat attributed to BYOD. Student newspaper The Vanderbilt Hustler cited posts on campus social network Fizz showing the message. "You have been compromised by BYOD," the recording said. "We suggest you reach out to us as soon as possible. Instructions have been placed on your desktop. Failure to communicate will result in this estate being brought to the ground completely. Make the right choice or rot with the wrong one." By Monday evening, Vanderbilt had restored access to campus Wi-Fi, but warned that access to most systems remains restricted. "We know this has disrupted important work and caused frustration across the university," it said . "Vanderbilt Information Technology is working with government agencies and other partners to manage this situation." Students were told to attend classes as scheduled on Tuesday and contact instructors about flexibility on coursework deadlines. Staff were instructed to report to work normally. Vanderbilt's Athletics department said that its ticketing system was unavailable, and that students were unable to claim tickets for the college's football game against Alabama on Saturday. BYOD claimed responsibility for the attack on Vanderbilt on Monday, along with extensive data theft. "If you could not tell already, your databases are locked [and] we have your entire estate and research data," it said via its leak site. "Over 1 million SSNs, full names, email addresses, phone numbers, student and employee records, full takeover of your DC, whatever was on your network, we possess." Vanderbilt has not confirmed BYOD's claims about the extent of its access or the data allegedly stolen. BYOD may be a familiar name to some. The group previously claimed attacks on the University of New Mexico and Trump Mobile's customer database . BYOD also claimed responsibility on Monday for an attack on Texas Health and Human Services. The agency has not publicly confirmed an incident and did not immediately respond to our questions. ®

item.title: Total solar eclipse 2027 vs 2028 — Which one should you choose, Egypt or Australia?
item.description: null For those who want to experience a total solar eclipse, the next two years present the best kind of problem. On Aug. 2, 2027, the so-called "eclipse of the century " will sweep across southern Spain, North Africa and the Middle East, bringing more than six minutes of totality to parts of Egypt. Then, on July 22, 2028, another exceptionally long total solar eclipse will cross Australia, putting the remote Outback and Sydney Harbor in the path of the moon's dark central shadow before it reaches New Zealand's beautiful South Island. Both eclipses will be spectacular, and both will require careful planning, yet they promise very different experiences. The 2027 event combines over six minutes of totality with some of the very best weather prospects possible, while 2028 offers over five minutes of totality above some of the world's most famous wildernesses and cityscapes. Eclipse chasing requires careful planning and dedication, but also significant funds. If you can only choose one, which should it be? 2027 total solar eclipse: pros and cons A map of the 2027 total solar eclipse path. (Image credit: Michael Zeiler/EclipseAtlas.com) On paper, 2027 is difficult to beat. Maximum totality on Aug. 2 will last about 6 minutes, 23 seconds, making it the longest totality on land since 1991 and until 2114. The path of totality will cross southern Spain and Gibraltar before sweeping across Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Egypt, Sudan, Saudi Arabia, Yemen, Somalia and the Chagos Islands. About 88.9 million people live in its path, according to Time and Date . It will dominate the news for weeks. For Europeans, southern Spain is the obvious easy option. Tarifa, at the country's southern tip, will see about 4 minutes, 39 seconds of totality, while the U.K. Overseas Territory of Gibraltar gets about 4 minutes, 25 seconds. Travel farther east and the duration increases, with Sfax in Tunisia getting around 5 minutes, 41 seconds and locations in Egypt experiencing more than six minutes. Weather prospects generally improve, too, as the path crosses the deserts of North Africa. Egypt is the headline destination. Luxor will see about 6 minutes, 20 seconds of totality near midday, with Karnak Temple, the Valley of the Kings, and some of the world's greatest ancient monuments nearby. The climatic odds are excellent, with clouds extremely rare in early August. That combination of a very long totality, ancient landscapes and a very high probability of a clear sky makes 2027's path of totality highly unusual. But there are downsides. Temperatures around Luxor can exceed 105°F (41°C) in August, a dust storm is not impossible, and totality occurs shortly after 1 p.m. when the sun (and moon) will be high overhead — making photography very difficult. Demand is already intense, making organized trips expensive. Spain will be considerably easier and probably cheaper for European eclipse chasers, but at the expense of roughly two minutes of totality — and slightly less favora

item.title: How Heineken Created Immersive Experiences That Took Lagos Fashion Week 2026 Beyond the Runway
item.description: In a city where creativity is a culture and every corner has a story to tell, Heineken brought another expression of Lagos to life at Lagos Fashion Week 2026 . Through its City of Cities: Where Taste Rules experience, the brand transformed its eleven-year partnership with the fashion showcase into a celebration of the people, ideas, and experiences shaping the city’s creative identity, bringing fashion, music, innovation, and social connections together across the week. From runway presentations to the Heineken Lounge, the debut of Heineken Studio, and an energetic after-party, the brand created experiences that went beyond the collections on display, inviting guests to explore new expressions of taste, discover creative possibilities, and connect over shared interests. At the heart of the experience was City of Cities: Where Taste Rules, an experience inspired by the many influences that make Lagos what it is. First introduced in 2025, the concept recognises that Lagos is more than one city; it is a melting pot of different cultures, communities, sounds, and styles. At Lagos Fashion Week 2026, Heineken brought this idea into focus, celebrating the diversity of expression that makes the city’s creative scene distinct. The experience also marked another chapter in Heineken’s eleven-year journey with Lagos Fashion Week. Over the years, the partnership has explored the intersection of fashion, craftsmanship, and taste through initiatives such as Woven Threads in 2022, the Dyelab collaboration in 2023, and the H45 Collection in 2024, before introducing City of Cities: Where Taste Rules in 2025. Each edition has created a new way to engage with fashion and culture, with this year’s experience building on that foundation through fresh expressions of creativity and innovation. Aligned with the 2026 theme, CRAFTED: Heritage. Innovation. Circular Futures, Heineken’s presence celebrated the artistry, intentionality, and evolving perspectives shaping contemporary fashion. Across the venue, guests arrived in style, adding their own interpretations of fashion and self-expression to the atmosphere. The Heineken Lounge provided a space to unwind, exchange ideas, and connect as guests enjoyed chilled Heineken, refreshments, and the runway presentations. The experience also offered a taste of something different, with guests exploring Foam Infusions in exciting variations, including espresso and blood orange. A major highlight was the Nigerian debut of Heineken Studio, the brand’s Playground of Innovation, which brought together taste, creativity, and personal expression in an interactive space. Beyond discovering new ways to experience lager through Foam Infusions, guests could step into the painting studio to create personalised designs on their own Heineken cans. The photo area and Heineken-branded backdrops also became popular spots for guests to capture their moments, express their individual styles, and share their experiences. item.title: Smart meters to cost the UK billions: 2G switch-off means replacing 12-13 million
item.description: Between 12 and 13 million UK smart meters could stop working properly when 2G and 3G networks are switched off by 2033, and replacing them all is likely to cost around £4 billion ($5.3 billion). Smart meters have long been a controversial topic thanks to the British government's botched rollout of the technology; they were supposed to be fitted into 80 percent of households by 2020. But numerous delays and technical hitches, such as consumers finding their meter stopped being smart if they switched energy supplier , hindered progress. Now, a report from connectivity biz Wirepas, "The European Connectivity Trilemma," shows that it isn't just Brits who have problems, but that other European countries also have their share of smart meter issues and that no two countries have adopted the same approach. The UK's issues center on the fact that early meters used 2G or 3G cellular connections to transmit energy usage back to the supplier. These continued to be fitted until 4G versions began arriving at the end of 2024, the report says. This issue was covered by The Register back in 2023 , and again in 2024 . However, the government had already announced measures to phase out 2G and 3G networks by 2033 several years earlier, back in 2021, so it was known that any meters being fitted would have a limited lifespan. In fact, 3G services have now already been withdrawn by the networks , and they all plan to phase out 2G ahead of the 2033 deadline . BT/EE will begin closing its network from May 2029, VMO2 will start the same summer, and Vodafone aims to switch off in spring 2030. The report claims the UK now faces two substantial areas of expenditure as a result. The first covers newer, second generation (SMETS2) meters, where only the communications module needs swapping out, but even this is likely to cost £1.3 to £1.4 billion (c $1.7 to $1.9 billion) before the hardware cost of each new hub is even factored in. The other is for an estimated 7 million older, first-generation (SMETS1) meter installations, which have the cellular comms hard-wired in, so the whole meter typically needs replacing. The report authors estimate this will cost another £2.1 billion to £2.45 billion ($2.8 billion to $3.3 billion), at an indicative replacement cost of £300 to £350 per installation. This results in the estimated £4 billion in gross replacement costs, which will ultimately feed into household energy bills, adding to the very costs the government is currently trying to reduce. We asked the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ), which oversees smart meters, for comment. While some of these older meters would naturally have been due for replacement as part of normal asset renewal cycles, the cell network shutdown makes the replacement program unavoidable and dictates when much of the expenditure must occur. According to the report, the SMETS2 replacement largely applies to central and southern Britain, as second-gen meters in the north use a long-range radio n

item.title: All active Escape From Tarkov codes and rewards

item.title: 11 dead, dozens injured in motorway pileup
item.description: Eleven people died and dozens were injured on Tuesday in a mass pileup on a motorway in southeastern Bulgaria, whose roads rank as the most dangerous in the EU. Crashes in thick fog snared dozens of vehicles heading in both directions of the highway linking the capital Sofia to the Black Sea city of Burgas. An estimated 50 cars and trucks were involved in the accident near the city of Yambol, regional governor Georgi Chalakov told the BTA state news agency, as government officials rushed to the scene. Images showed overturned and smashed cars and trucks mangled together, as well as burnt-out vehicles. “The toll at this point is 11 dead and 48 injured,” Prime Minister Rumen Radev told reporters. Radev was meeting EU chief Ursula von der Leyen, who is on a visit to Bulgaria, but the prime minister cancelled his official events scheduled for later Tuesday. The injured were transported to hospitals in nearby cities. The government dispatched two aircraft equipped with stretchers and medical teams. Bulgaria saw 71 road fatalities per million inhabitants in 2025, the highest rate in the European Union, according to European Commission figures. Victims blame the Balkan nation’s high number of traffic deaths on reckless driving, poorly maintained roads and an inefficient justice system. Stricter penalties Romanian Foreign Minister Dan Neculaescu said one Romanian was among the injured and expressed “deepest condolences” to the victims and their families in a post on X. European Council chief Antonio Costa also said on X he was “deeply saddened to learn of the tragic traffic accident in Bulgaria this morning”. A total of 456 people were killed in road traffic accidents in Bulgaria in 2025 — down five percent from the previous year and 27 percent lower than in 2019. The EU in 2019 introduced a target to reduce road deaths and serious injuries by 50 percent by 2030. A European Commission report in October said that although the EU remains “one of the world’s safest regions for road travel”, the majority of member states were not yet on track to meet the safety target. The report said that just five of the EU’s 27 countries — including Bulgaria — were on track to meet the target. However, “despite their progress since 2019, Bulgaria and Romania, alongside Croatia, continue to have the highest fatality rates in the EU when measuring deaths per million inhabitants”, the report said. In 2023, Bulgaria’s parliament adopted stricter penalties for anyone found to be driving under the influence of drugs. The cars of accused drivers are now impounded until the trial, even when the suspects have no previous criminal record. Bulgaria’s busy road traffic due to its position as a gateway to the EU is one of the main factors behind the high accident rate, according to experts. But Bulgaria’s status as the EU’s poorest member state also plays a role, with around half of the cars registered more than 20 years old. Vanguard News The post 11 dead, dozens injured in motorway

item.title: Only 36% of Nigerians have access to improved toilets — FG
item.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government has disclosed that less than 36 per cent of Nigerians have access to improved toilet facilities, raising concerns over persistent sanitation challenges and the associated public health risks. The Minister of Environment, Balarabe Abbas Lawal, disclosed this on Tuesday during a press briefing in Abuja to commemorate the 2026 World Toilet Day. Lawal, who was represented by the Director of Pollution Control and Environmental Health, Mrs Omotunde Adeola, said many public places, including markets, motor parks, schools and communities, still lacked adequate and functional toilet facilities. He warned that the situation was contributing to open defecation, contamination of food and water sources, and the spread of sanitation-related diseases such as cholera and typhoid. According to him, inadequate sanitation poses serious threats to public health, environmental safety and human dignity. The minister said women, girls, children, older persons and persons living with disabilities were particularly affected by the shortage of appropriate sanitation facilities. He stressed that no child should miss school because of inadequate toilet facilities, while no woman or girl should be forced to compromise her safety and dignity because of the absence of suitable toilets. Providing a global perspective, Lawal said about 4.5 billion people worldwide still lacked safely managed sanitation, while 892 million continued to practise open defecation. He said the figures underscored the need to accelerate efforts towards achieving the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly those relating to clean water and sanitation, gender equality, good health and sustainable communities by 2030. Government interventions On efforts to address the challenge, the minister said the Federal Ministry of Environment, in collaboration with relevant ministries, state governments and development partners, was implementing programmes to improve sanitation and promote safe excreta disposal nationwide. He listed the initiatives to include capacity building for Environmental Health Officers on faecal sludge management and toilet design, the Clean and Green Programme, and the Community-Based Waste Management and Open Defecation Control Programme. Other interventions, he said, included integrating sanitation into climate adaptation and circular economy initiatives, as well as partnering with private sector operators to provide environmentally friendly sanitation facilities. Lawal announced that the ministry would convene a National Dialogue on Faecal Sludge Management on November 23, 2026, involving seven selected states across the six geopolitical zones and the Federal Capital Territory. He said the dialogue would enable participating states to assess their experiences, share challenges and develop practical recommendations for improving faecal sludge management. item.title: MOSOP accuses Niger Delta governors of mismanaging 13% derivation funds
item.description: ….Group calls for amendment of derivation law, commends NDDC’s development efforts By Daniel Abia PORT HARCOURT — The Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People (MOSOP) has accused successive governors in the Niger Delta of mismanaging the 13 per cent derivation funds, calling for an amendment of the law to ensure that oil-producing communities directly benefit from the revenue. MOSOP President, Fegalo Nsuke, made the call on Tuesday in Port Harcourt during activities marking the 31st anniversary of the execution of environmental activist Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other Ogoni leaders by the military government of the late General Sani Abacha. Nsuke said the objectives of the derivation fund had not been achieved because state governors allegedly exercised excessive discretion over its allocation, rather than directing the resources to communities where oil and gas were extracted. He argued that the sacrifices of Saro-Wiwa and other Ogoni martyrs would have limited impact on the lives of people unless laws governing resource benefits specifically addressed the needs of communities bearing the consequences of oil exploration. “The idea of derivation funds was to address the underdevelopment in the Niger Delta region. However, the structure of administration of the funds makes it vulnerable to abuse and has left the funds at the discretion of state governors. This needs to be addressed,” he said. According to Nsuke, the intention behind the derivation arrangement was to address underdevelopment in oil-producing areas, but the funds were not being adequately directed towards those communities. Citing Ogba/Egbema and Andoni communities in Rivers State, he said areas responsible for significant oil production had yet to receive what he considered adequate development funding. He argued that allowing governors to determine spending priorities without directly channelling an appropriate share to oil-producing communities had undermined the objectives of the derivation arrangement. Commends NDDC Despite his criticism of the management of derivation funds, Nsuke commended the current management of the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) for what he described as its visible development impact across the region. He urged the commission to sustain and expand its interventions, noting that the agency emerged from the struggles for justice and development championed by Saro-Wiwa and other Niger Delta activists. “It is important that the areas from where resources are extracted should get their due rewards and a proportionate injection of the derivation funds. The structure for the administration of the derivation funds needs to change if we must achieve that. “I am pleased that the NDDC under its present management is making some impressive impacts. MOSOP will encourage them to do more,” he said. item.title: Ukraine’s fiber-optic drones get squeezed by AI data center demand
item.description: Impervious to battlefield jamming, drones physically connected to human operators by miles of fiber-optic cables have become such a common weapon of war in Ukraine that trees and fields are strewn with tangled cables thinner than fishing lines. But importing such fiber-optic material from China has become more costly as drone warfare’s needs compete with global demand from AI data centers for the same limited supply—and so Ukrainian drone makers have been adapting. Since the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022, the Ukrainians have been forced out of necessity to continually develop battlefield innovations involving first-person view (FPV) quadcopter drones and other heavier types of drones. But it was the Russian military that first deployed unjammable fiber-optic drones to repel Ukrainian forces’ cross-border incursion into the Kursk Oblast in 2024. The Ukrainians quickly followed suit in developing their own fiber-optic drones, given the drones’ capability to shrug off electronic warfare jamming that could neutralize radio-controlled drones. Russia and Ukraine have relied on Chinese suppliers for some off-the-shelf drones and a wide array of drone components, including bulk orders of fiber wound around very large spools or sometimes small finished spools ready for installation on drones. The finished spools can hold enough fiber-optic cable for drones to regularly operate at ranges of dozens of miles, and sometimes up to 62 miles (100 kilometers) in extreme cases, as reported by the independent Russian publication The Insider . item.title: Troops rescue three kidnap victims, kill two terrorists in Adamawa
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK) have rescued three kidnapped civilians and killed two terrorists in separate operations in Adamawa State. The troops also recovered two AK-47 rifles, ammunition, locally fabricated explosive devices, stolen vehicles and farm produce belonging to residents who narrowly escaped abduction. The Acting Media Information Officer of OPHK, Capt. Mohammed Goni, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday. He said the three victims were rescued by troops deployed in Mubi following a distress call from farmers around Dutse-Uku in Mubi South Local Government Area. According to him, suspected kidnappers abducted a farmer, identified as Happiness Dama Dauda, on November 9 while she was working on her farm and also stole her motorcycle. Goni said the troops, working with local hunters, mobilised to the area and mounted pressure on the kidnappers, forcing them to abandon their victim and flee. He added that a sustained pursuit led to the rescue of two other residents suspected to have been abducted earlier, bringing the number of rescued victims to three. The troops also recovered a motorcycle, a tricycle conveying 15 bags of beans and a Hi-Jet pickup carrying 13 bags of groundnuts belonging to other farmers who narrowly escaped abduction. Goni said the respective village heads identified the recovered items, which were subsequently handed over to their owners. Two terrorists killed in Gombi In a separate operation on November 8, troops deployed at Zangula Kilba Junction in Gombi Local Government Area foiled an attempted attack by suspected Boko Haram/Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) terrorists. Two terrorists were killed during the encounter, while others fled following what the military described as the troops’ superior combat readiness and tactical resilience. Items recovered from the fleeing insurgents included two AK-47 rifles, four magazines, 115 rounds of ammunition, three belts of empty ammunition links and two cases of locally fabricated explosive devices. Other recovered items included a pair of desert boots, a backpack, an Android phone, a wristwatch and N15,000. Goni said troops had commenced exploitation operations to track down the fleeing terrorists and prevent them from regrouping. He added that troops were maintaining aggressive patrols and surveillance across the affected areas to prevent further attacks and reassure residents of their safety. The military urged residents to provide timely and credible intelligence to security agencies, stressing that collaboration between troops and local communities remained critical to tackling terrorism and other security threats. Operation Hadin Kai reaffirmed its commitment to sustaining operational pressure on terrorists and their collaborators to deny them the freedom to threaten the security and livelihoods of residents across the North-East. item.title: Madonna University: 15 nursing students beg for expulsion, suspension reversal over TikTok video
item.description: By Chioma Okoye Fifteen nursing students of Madonna University, Nigeria, have appealed to the university management to reverse their expulsion and suspension over a controversial TikTok video recorded during their community posting, pleading for another opportunity to complete their studies. The students, in a letter dated November 2, 2026, tendered an unreserved apology to the management, admitting that their conduct was unethical and had brought disrepute to the nursing profession and the university community. The video, which went viral on social media, sparked widespread reactions and prompted disciplinary action by the university management. In the appeal addressed to the university management through the Registrar, the students said they had reflected deeply on their actions and were genuinely remorseful. “We sincerely regret our said actions and assure the University Management and all relevant authorities that such an incident will not repeat itself again,” they said. They pleaded with the management to reconsider its decision, stressing that their families had made significant sacrifices to support their education and enable them to reach the present stage of their academic journey. The students said reversing the expulsion would give them an opportunity to complete their programmes and pursue their chosen professional careers instead of having their academic aspirations cut short. They also appreciated the university management for engaging with their parents and guardians and allowing them to present their concerns. According to the students, they did not take the gesture for granted and remained grateful for the opportunity given to their families to be heard. The appeal, jointly signed by the 15 students, urged the university management to reconsider the punishment and give them a second chance. item.title: Tinubu’s achievements will make it difficult to unseat him – Wike
item.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, says it will be immensely difficult for opposition parties to unseat President Bola Tinubu in the upcoming 2027 general elections. Wike said this in Abuja on Tuesday, after inspecting some ongoing projects within the federal capital territory. He cited what he described as Tinubu’s undeniable and rich report card of infrastructure development across the country. The minister said that the volume and pace of visible achievements delivered under Tinubu’s administration left very little room for political detractors to challenge the ruling party’s record. “You can see clearly that it will be difficult to unseat the president today because the report card is obvious in terms of what he has done. “Like I told you, this is our campaign. People ask what we are going to campaign with, but we have so many visible achievements all around us. “There is no way residents of Abuja will see the kind of infrastructure we have provided and say they are not happy with the achievements of Mr President. It is second to none,” he said. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the minister inspected the ongoing construction of Innet Southern Motorway, from the Area 1 roundabout to the Games Village bridges and Southern Parkway, linking Oladipo Diya Road with Ring Road II. He also inspected the ongoing construction of the Arterial Road S1 project in Abuja to connect Ring Road II to the FCT Fire Service Station in the Kaura and Gaduwa district corridors. Highlighting the rapid speed of execution on several key projects in the territory, Wike referenced the rapid transformation of the Southern Parkway project, which was flagged during the celebration of Tinubu’s third year in office. “Within six to seven months, you can see what has been achieved. “It is unimaginable, and that is why we are very happy,” Wike said. He pledged that the FCT administration remained on track to inaugurate at least 10 high-impact projects before the general elections scheduled for Jan. 16, 2027. item.title: Zamfara APC crisis deepens as aspirant petitions NEC, security agencies
item.description: …Yilwatda dismisses allegations as unfounded By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — The crisis in the Zamfara State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has taken a fresh turn, following a petition by an aspirant to the party’s National Executive Committee (NEC), National Working Committee (NWC) and security agencies over the composition of a committee to conduct a court-ordered fresh primary election. The primary is for the Kaura Namoda/Birnin Magaji Federal Constituency following an order by the Court of Appeal. The aspirant, Honourable Hassan Umar Dangaladima, accused the party’s National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, of unilaterally constituting the committee without involving the NWC. He alleged that the committee’s composition raised concerns about its impartiality and called on the party leadership to review the arrangement before the fresh primary. In the petition, Dangaladima claimed that no NWC meeting was convened to deliberate on or approve the committee’s composition and that neither the aspirants nor the Zamfara State chapter and other relevant stakeholders were consulted. However, Yilwatda, through his Special Adviser on Media and Strategic Communication, Abimbola Tooki, dismissed the allegations as unfounded. He said the claims did not reflect the party’s established decision-making process, insisting that the NWC operated as a collective body. “The National Chairman does not operate in isolation. He works in consultation and collaboration with other members of the NWC, and decisions are taken collectively in accordance with the party’s constitution, established procedures and internal mechanisms,” Tooki said. He described the suggestion that Yilwatda single-handedly constituted the committee without the knowledge or involvement of the NWC as misleading. According to him, the APC remains committed to respecting the rule of law, implementing court directives and ensuring that its internal processes are transparent, fair and credible. “The APC is a democratic institution governed by rules and collective responsibility, not the personal preferences of any individual,” he said. Alleges committee bias Dangaladima, however, maintained that the committee’s composition raised concerns about a possible conflict of interest. He alleged that some members were loyalists, supporters or agents of another aspirant, Honourable Aminu Sani Jaji, whom he described as his main rival in the contest. The petitioner also challenged Jaji’s eligibility, alleging that his name was not contained in the APC membership register for Birnin Magaji Ward submitted to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). He said he obtained a Certified True Copy of the register from INEC, which he attached to his petition as evidence. Dangaladima further claimed that the party had been formally notified of the alleged membership irregularity through a letter dated November 4, 2026, from his solicitors, Trinity Chambers, led by D.C. item.title: Review: Apple's M6 MacBook Pro is good, but it's missing all the exciting stuff
item.description: I've written more than once about the weird positioning of Apple's entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro, which has always occupied an uncomfortable perch between the MacBook Air and the higher-end MacBook Pros. The best versions of this laptop, like last year's M5 refresh, come with the same basic design and external features of the higher-end MacBook Pros, just with a more modest processor and a lower ceiling for specs like RAM and storage. The lesser versions stick with older designs or other compromises, reserving Apple's most updated designs and screen technologies for the more expensive high-end models. Recall the 13-inch M1 and M2 MacBook Pros, which stuck with Apple's 2016-era MacBook Pro designs for everything , up to and including the now-abandoned Touch Bar. (If you're someone at Apple maintaining Touch Bar support into the 2030s for the sake of these two laptop models, I'd like to hear from you. Not for a story! I'd just like to know how you are.) This year's entry-level MacBook Pro mostly falls into that latter category. It does get an Apple M6 chip, and the M6 is great—rumors suggest the M6 won't get Pro, Max, or Ultra configurations, so there are some fringe benefits here that you can't get in the top-tier MacBook Pros. But it uses the same MacBook Pro design Apple has been using since 2021 . There's no touchscreen, no OLED panel, no Dynamic Island, no half-pound weight reduction, no glowing Apple logo on the lid. item.title: Google DeepMind melds humans and AI agents to vet Signal's secure messaging techniques
item.description: Google DeepMind researchers have completed a formal verification of Signal's messaging security, marking what they claim is the first time AI has helped devise a proof that links protocol-level security guarantees to a widely used cryptographic implementation. They did so using AlphaProof Code, a multi-agent framework for formal software specification and verification. AlphaProof Code relies on a human-guided agent that writes a Lean specification, assesses machine code semantics, and crafts an agent-authored proof that the Lean kernel checks against the specification. In this instance, AlphaProof Code verified Signal’s post-quantum PQXDH handshake and Triple Ratchet , thereby validating the design of libsignal 's forward secrecy, authentication, post-compromise security, and handshake secrecy. In so doing, the Google/DeepMind team – Swarat Chaudhuri, Andrew Ferraiuolo, Anton Kovsharov, Tej Chajed, Sam Schlesinger, Karn Seth, Jonathan Katz, Charles Sutton, and Pushmeet Kohli – has taken a step toward a challenge the Beneficial AI Foundation issued in April to formally verify the Signal protocol and Signal app with Lean. The AlphaProof Code process involves working with various models to turn Signal's security goals into a human-reviewed mathematical specification. Based on this spec, the researchers assigned Gemini Carbon agents to generate Lean code proving the correctness of the libsignal implementation. After the agents generated 6.5 million lines of Lean code, they undertook an auditing pass and flagged bits that required human review. The result is theoretical in that it assumes perfect cryptography and doesn't guarantee the computational secrecy of bytes. But it's still a meaningful assertion of correctness. "It's a system that is fundamentally built for human AI collaboration," said Swarat Chaudhuri, research scientist at Google DeepMind and a professor at the University of Texas at Austin, in an interview with The Register . Traditionally, said Chaudhuri, you start proving theorems with well-defined problems formulated by a mathematician that get submitted to an AI agent for proof. In this case, the researchers had to figure out what to prove. "In formal methods, we always had this belief that verification is the hard bit," he said. "There's thirty or forty years of work on how to scale up verification. Now we are able to do that. So now the question is what are we verifying? … That process is fundamentally human-in-the-loop, but we devised a process of trying to scale it up to the extent possible with AI." As Chaudhuri and his colleagues note in their research paper, "AlphaProof Code: Verifying Signal’s Security at the Machine-Code Level," formal verification used to require heroic efforts. Formally verifying the seL4 microkernel took 20 person-years, while developing the verified CompCert C compiler took six years. AlphaProof Code, they believe, can drastically reduce the cost of formal verification, though their Signal work still took

item.title: Gombe records 98 road crash deaths, 1,345 injuries in nine months — FRSC
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe GOMBE — The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) has disclosed that 98 persons were killed while 1,345 others sustained injuries in road traffic crashes recorded across Gombe State between January and September 2026. The FRSC Sector Commander in the state, Commander Samson Kaura, disclosed this on Tuesday in Gombe while addressing members of the Gombe State Council of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) during the commemoration of the 2026 World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims. Kaura said the command recorded 1,345 road traffic incidents during the nine-month period, adding that fatalities increased by six per cent compared with the corresponding period. He identified excessive speeding and reckless driving as major causes of road crashes and fatalities, warning that irresponsible road use continued to pose a serious threat to motorists and other road users. According to him, the annual World Day of Remembrance provides an opportunity to honour those who have lost their lives or sustained serious injuries in road crashes, while drawing attention to the need for stronger legal responses to traffic offences resulting in deaths and injuries. He said the commemoration also seeks to promote better support for crash victims and their families, as well as evidence-based interventions to prevent and ultimately eliminate road traffic deaths and injuries. The sector commander expressed concern that the fatalities recorded in the first nine months of 2026 had surpassed the figure for the whole of 2025. He said the command recorded 1,614 road traffic incidents in 2025, resulting in 92 deaths and 926 injuries. Kaura described the 2026 World Day of Remembrance as a campaign aimed at translating remembrance into concrete action, stressing the need for collective responsibility in addressing road traffic crashes. In his response, the Vice Chairman of the Gombe State NUJ Council, Emmanuel Akila, who represented the state chairman, Faruk Muazu Gombe, pledged the union’s continued cooperation with the FRSC in promoting road safety and development. Akila, however, urged the FRSC to strengthen collaboration with the union to identify and curb the activities of fake journalists in the state. He called on the corps to insist on proper identification of journalists during official engagements and other road-related activities to prevent impersonation and protect the integrity of the journalism profession. The NUJ vice chairman also urged the FRSC to intensify enforcement against vehicle overloading, describing the practice as one of the factors contributing to fatalities in road crashes. He stressed the need for sustained public enlightenment, effective enforcement of traffic regulations and stronger collaboration among relevant stakeholders to reduce road crashes and safeguard lives on the highways. item.title: UK, Nigeria seal $750m infrastructure deal as Pension funds prepare to unlock billions
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young Nigeria and the United Kingdom have strengthened their economic partnership with a proposed $750 million infrastructure investment fund aimed at mobilising billions of dollars in pension assets to finance critical development projects across Nigeria and other selected African markets. The initiative, which has already attracted interest from 19 Nigerian pension funds, is expected to channel long-term domestic and international investments into key sectors, including energy, transportation and digital infrastructure, as both countries seek to address the continent’s widening infrastructure financing gap. A statement from PenCom disclosed that the agreement was signed by Nigeria’s Pension Industry Leadership Council, PILC,and UK-funded specialist development agency, FSD Africa, in Lagos on November 10, 2026. Under the agreement, FSD Africa will provide technical expertise and advisory support to PILC towards establishing the proposed investment platform, including the selection of a fund manager through a competitive process, engagement with prospective investors and development finance institutions, capacity building and support for necessary regulatory reforms. The initiative was developed by Nigerian Pension Fund Administrators, PFAs, with support from the National Pension Commission, PenCom, and FSD Africa. Speaking on the development, UK Deputy High Commissioner in Lagos, Jonny Baxter, said the partnership reflected the shared commitment of both countries to mobilising domestic capital, particularly pension funds, for productive investment in the real economy. According to him: “The UK is proud to partner with the Nigeria’s Pension Industry and the pensions regulator Pencom to progress this investment. Both our countries are prioritising tacking the challenge of attracting more domestic capital, including from pension funds, into the real economy. It is great to see Nigeria making concrete progress on its efforts and be a part of those opportunities to turn this ambition into investment, jobs, and economic growth.” On her part, Chair of the Nigeria Pension Industry Leadership Council and Director-General of the National Pension Commission, Ms Omolola Oloworaran, described the proposed investment platform as timely, stressing that the pension industry was committed to deploying its substantial pool of long-term savings towards national development while protecting contributors’ retirement funds. She said: “The pension industry holds the largest pool of long-term savings capital in the country, and we are committed to mobilising it to deepen infrastructure development, while safeguarding the retirement savings of contributors. This MoU is the first step we are taking as an industry, and it is just the beginning.” In the same vein, Chief Executive Officer of FSD Africa, Mark Napier, said the initiative would help address the contradiction between Africa’s substantial institutional capital and its huge infrastructure financi

item.title: Ologe highlights growing importance of risk leadership in digital business
item.description: Mojisola Ologe, an Associate Chartered Risk Manager, has highlighted the growing importance of risk management in strengthening corporate governance, business performance and operational resilience amid increasing digitalisation. Ologe, who received the professional designation from the Chartered Risk Management Institute of Nigeria (CRMI) on October 15, 2026, said effective risk management was becoming increasingly important as organisations expanded their reliance on technology and digital services. She noted that decisions involving access to information systems, introduction of new services, third-party dependencies and business recovery arrangements could have direct implications for customers, regulatory compliance and organisational credibility. Her professional experience spans consulting, banking and digital payments, including roles at Phillips Consulting and Sterling Bank, where she worked across technology assurance, information technology risk and control, business continuity and compliance oversight. The experience, according to her, has reinforced the need to translate identified operational and technological weaknesses into practical business implications and corrective actions. Ologe currently serves as Chief Risk and Compliance Officer at Hydrogen Payment Services Limited, where her responsibilities cover enterprise risk management, regulatory compliance, cybersecurity governance and operational resilience. In the digital payments sector, these areas are closely interconnected, as disruptions to technology systems can quickly affect customer services, expose businesses to financial losses and create regulatory challenges. Effective risk management, therefore, goes beyond identifying potential threats to understanding business operations, assessing critical dependencies and ensuring that management takes timely corrective action. Clear accountability, appropriate internal controls and effective escalation mechanisms are also essential to helping organisations address vulnerabilities while pursuing their business objectives. Ologe’s professional recognition by CRMI underscores the importance of continuous professional development in the risk management sector, particularly as emerging technologies and changing business conditions create new operational and regulatory challenges. Risk professionals, increasingly, are expected to contribute beyond compliance monitoring by providing insights that inform corporate strategy, investment decisions and everyday business operations. Their role, the profile noted, is to help organisations pursue growth while maintaining a clear understanding of potential exposures and strengthening their capacity to withstand disruptions.
